manual.mchjong.category.mcr.description: MCR scores by patterns. A win needs at least 8 points, and flowers add points per tile. This chapter covers tiles and flowers, winning, calls, special hands, and how patterns combine and are paid, then lists every pattern by value.

manual.mchjong.category.riichi.descripti: Riichi mahjong needs at least one yaku to win, and a closed hand may declare riichi. This chapter covers tiles, winning, calls, riichi, draws and scoring, then lists every yaku and yakuman and explains how three-player mahjong and the rule presets differ.
manual.mchjong.category.riichi.name: Riichi Mahjong
manual.mchjong.category.sichuan.descript: Sichuan mahjong uses three suits, has no chows and starts with each player voiding a suit. When one player wins the others play on, called Blood Battle. This chapter covers voids, wins, the dealer, fan, kong payments and draws, then compares the two presets.

manual.mchjong.category.taiwan.descripti: In Taiwanese mahjong each player is dealt 16 tiles, a win needs five melds and a pair, and hands are settled in tai. This chapter covers the deal, flowers, calls, declaring ready and payments, then lists every tai pattern.
manual.mchjong.category.taiwan.name: Taiwanese Mahjong
manual.mchjong.entry.automatic_table.int: An $(bold)automatic mahjong table$() is a table whose machinery does the manual steps for you. Once players are seated, it shuffles, builds the wall, opens it, deals and draws by itself and assigns seats directly, so players only choose the tiles to discard and the actions to declare.
An ordinary table needs the players to do these steps by hand. See $(l:handling)Manual Table Handling$(/l). An automatic table also does not need dice or scoring supplies in the mahjong box.
The rest of the table works like an ordinary one. It needs a table cloth, a mahjong box in its storage slot, and a game and rules chosen in the lobby.
manual.mchjong.entry.automatic_table.upg: In a crafting table, arrange the materials as shown above to upgrade an empty ordinary mahjong table to an automatic one, which keeps its original wood and name.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.declare: In Riichi mahjong, click the Riichi button while in tenpai and then click a highlighted tile to discard it and declare riichi. In Taiwanese mahjong, click the Declare Ready button and discard a highlighted tile to declare ready. Right-click or press the Esc key before discarding to cancel.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.discard: On your turn, click a tile in your hand to discard it. Under the Discard Input setting in personal settings, choose the Single Click or Double Click option.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.discard.co: When you can chi, pon, kan or win, buttons appear beside your hand. Click a button to choose the action, then click the tiles to use if there is more than one combination. Click the Pass button to decline. Right-click or press the Esc key to cancel the current selection.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.name: Table Controls
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.view: The view button on the toolbar switches between Seated View and Immersive View. Hold the right mouse button and drag to look around, and scroll to zoom. Personal settings adjust the camera distance and height and can reset the view direction.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.view.conti: To leave your seat, press Esc to close the table screen and then press the sneak key.$(br2)To watch a match, walk around the table and look at the tiles and displays in the world. While watching, right-clicking the table shows a hint.
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.name: Personal Settings
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.packs: Custom tile faces, backs, riichi sticks and voices can be packaged as ZIP presets in the faces, backs, sticks and voices folders under config/mchjong/presets in the game directory. Joining a server with preset sharing enabled downloads its presets automatically.
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.setti: Click the Settings button on the toolbar, select the Personal category on the left, then open the Personal Settings option to adjust the view, table animations, discard input, hand and river display, and effect and voice volumes.

The Personal Presets option in the same category selects the riichi-stick appearance and match voice.$(br2)The host manages the settings in the Room category. Only operators can change the settings in the World category.
Away from a table, open Personal Settings and Personal Presets through Mod Menu on Fabric or the Mods screen on Forge and NeoForge.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.cloth: A $(bold)table cloth$() is the felt laid on a mahjong table, and a table without one cannot start a match. Right-click the table while holding a table cloth to lay it. The tabletop takes the color of the cloth. A cloth already on the table returns to your inventory.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.cloth.con: To take the cloth back, sneak and right-click the top of the table with empty hands. The cloth can only be changed or removed while no match is running. During a match, a message asks you to end the match first. Once players are seated, only members of that room may change it, and you must stand within eight blocks of the table.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.manual: The $(bold)Mahjong Manual$() is the book you are reading, and it is available only when Patchouli is installed. Each player receives one the first time they join a world. A lost copy can be crafted from a book, green dye and a mahjong tile. Its recipe is drawn beside this page with the table cloth.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.manual.co: In the Match Rules screens, every rule option has a ? button. It opens an explanation, and the Handbook button there turns to the manual page for that rule. Clicking an award on a results screen opens its explanation in the same way.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.name: Setting Up a Table
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.placement: A $(bold)mahjong table$() is the block on which a match is played. Place it where its center should be. The 3 by 3 area around the center and the layer above must be free of blocks and liquids, and the block below the center must be solid. Otherwise a message says the table needs a clear flat area.

A placed table also occupies the eight surrounding spaces. Breaking it drops its cloth, mahjong boxes and the sticks or cards in its drawers as items, and a match in progress at the table is lost. $(l:automatic_table)Automatic tables$(/l) are placed in the same way.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.recipes: Mahjong tables, stools and table cloths are all crafted in a crafting table. A $(bold)mahjong table$() takes five slabs and two fences of one wood, any of the 11 vanilla wood types, and the table keeps that wood. The recipe grids beside this page show the table and the stool.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.recipes.c: A $(bold)mahjong stool$() takes two carpets, two slabs and two fences and yields two stools. The seat takes the color of the carpets, and the slabs and fences decide the wood. A $(bold)table cloth$() takes three carpets of one color laid in a row and yields one cloth of that color. Its grid is on the last page of this entry.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.stools: A $(bold)mahjong stool$() is the seat beside a table. Place it exactly two blocks from the table's center to the north, south, east or west, which puts it against the edge of the 3 by 3 tabletop. A stool anywhere else belongs to no table.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.stools.co: Every seat taken by a human player needs a stool, while seats filled by computer players need none. A four-player match therefore needs up to four stools, and three-player mahjong up to three without the west seat. Right-click an empty stool without sneaking to sit down. $(l:seating)Starting a Match$(/l) describes what happens next.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.storage: The $(bold)table storage$() is the pair of slots inside a table that hold mahjong boxes, labeled Case 1 and Case 2. While no match is running, right-click the table with empty hands or with a mahjong box in hand to open it. Sneaking and right-clicking with empty hands opens the table's lobby screen instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.storage.c: When a match starts, the table checks the two boxes one at a time and uses the first one that holds the complete set the rules need, marking it In use. A set must be complete within a single box, but dice, point sticks and scoring cards may be split between the two. The line below the slots names what is still missing, such as No tablecloth laid yet.

When the match begins, the table moves the required sticks or cards from the boxes into each seat's drawer and locks the storage. When the match ends, the drawers return to their starting contents and the storage opens again. An automatic table has no drawers and only needs the tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.collect: Settle point sticks or scoring cards by hand using the result screen's point changes. In Riichi mahjong, sweep your tiles to the center to continue.$(br2)When the match ends, drawers return to their starting contents.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.deal: To deal, drag the highlighted part of the wall into your hand. Each player takes four tiles three times and then one more, and the dealer takes a fourteenth tile and discards first.$(br2)During play, drag the highlighted wall tile into your hand when it is your turn to draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.manual: On an ordinary table, players shuffle, build the wall, break it and take their tiles by hand. Tiles to move are highlighted, and the prompt describes the current step. Press the Esc key to cancel a drag.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.manual.con: $(li)To shuffle, drag the face-down tiles on the tabletop.$(li)To build, drag highlighted tiles in front of you to form your wall.$(li)To break the wall, the dealer rolls the dice from the middle of the table once the walls are built and breaks the wall at the result.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.name: Manual Table Handling
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.maid: Touhou Little Maid adds little maids to the game. With it installed, you can set a maid's job to Mahjong so that she takes a seat and plays with you.
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.maid.continued: To prepare, set up a mahjong table with a cloth within her work area, leave an empty stool and take a seat first. During working hours the maid walks to an empty stool and sits down.
When the match starts she takes her assigned seat and plays. Changing her job makes her stand up at once and free the seat.
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.name: Touhou Little Maid
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.calls: A $(bold)chow$(), a $(bold)pung$() and a $(bold)melded kong$() are melds made with a tile another player has just discarded and laid face up in front of you. Such a meld is $(bold)melded$(). A chow joins the tile with two tiles of your hand into a sequence, and only the previous player's discard may be used.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.calls.con: A pung joins it with two identical tiles, and a melded kong with three. Both may use any player's discard.$(br2)After a chow or pung you discard a tile, and play continues with the player after you. Players who were skipped do not draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.kongs: A $(bold)kong$() is four identical tiles and is declared in one of three ways.$(li)A $(bold)melded kong$() uses another player's discard.$(li)A $(bold)concealed kong$() uses four identical tiles of your hand after you draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.kongs.con: $(li)An $(bold)added kong$() adds the fourth tile, held in your hand, to a pung you melded earlier, again after you draw.$(br2)After a chow or pung you must discard first, and once the wall is empty no kong can be declared.

After a kong, draw a replacement tile from the back of the wall and continue your turn. Winning on that tile is $(l:mcr_fan_middle#out_with_replacement_tile)Out with Replacement Tile$(/l). The kong patterns are in $(l:mcr_combining)Combining Patterns$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.name: Calls and Kongs
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.priority: When several players claim the same tile, the $(bold)claim priority$() decides. A win beats a pung or kong, and a pung or kong beats a chow. If several players win on one tile, the first in turn order after the discarder wins.
For example, player A discards. Player B, next in turn, wants a chow, player C a pung and player D a win. D's win is carried out. Without D's win, C's pung is carried out and B's chow is dropped. Once the wall is empty, the last discard can only be won. It cannot be claimed for a chow, pung or kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.robbing: $(bold)Robbing the kong$() is winning on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong. Before the added kong is completed, every player who can win declares, and the first in turn order after the player adding the tile wins. That player pays as the discarder.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_calls.robbing.c: If nobody wins, the added kong stands and the player draws the replacement tile. Melded and concealed kongs cannot be robbed. The value is on the card $(l:mcr_fan_middle#robbing_the_kong)Robbing the Kong$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_combining.combi: The patterns that apply to one hand are added into its points. For example, All Pungs (6 points) and Half Flush (6 points) that apply together make 12 points. This total is the number compared with the minimum in $(l:mcr_winning)Winning and the Minimum$(/l).

Three limits prevent double counting.$(li)A pattern already contained in a larger pattern is not counted again.$(li)The same tiles cannot be regrouped to count twice.$(li)In patterns built from sequences, a sequence not yet used may be combined once with one suitable sequence of a counted combination.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_combining.exclu: The notes on the pattern cards about patterns that are not counted are the results of these limits. For example, Mixed Triple Chow cannot also count Mixed Double Chow, and the sequences of a Pure Straight cannot count Short Straight or Two Terminal Chows.

A closed hand won by self-draw scores Fully Concealed Hand for 4 points, not also Concealed Hand (2) and Self-Drawn (1). When a hand can be divided in several ways, only the highest-scoring division counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_combining.kongs: Kong patterns depend only on the number of kongs and whether they are concealed, and each pattern is named for the kongs it needs.

An added kong counts as a melded kong, and a kong counts as a pung in any pattern that asks for pungs. The table shows the values of the five kong patterns. Three kongs and four kongs have their own cards, $(l:mcr_fan_high#three_kongs)Three Kongs$(/l) and $(l:mcr_fan_high#four_kongs)Four Kongs$(/l).

Pattern|Points
Melded Kong|1
Concealed Kong|2
Two Melded Kongs|4
Melded and Concealed Kong|6
Two Concealed Kongs|8
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_combining.name: Combining Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_ev: $(bold)All Even Pungs$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) and the pair only of 2, 4, 6 and 8. Does not count All Pungs, All Simples, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_gr: $(bold)All Green$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Only 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 of Bamboo and Green. Full Flush or Half Flush can also count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_ho: $(bold)All Honors$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Only honors. Does not count All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors, One Voided Suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_te: $(bold)All Terminals$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Only 1s and 9s. Does not count All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors, No Honors. A separate Double Pung can count.
$(bold)All Terminals and Honors$()$(br)32 points$(br2)Only 1s, 9s and honors. Does not count All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.big_fo: $(bold)Big Four Winds$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of East, South, West and North. Does not count Big Three Winds, Prevalent Wind, Seat Wind, Pung of Terminals or Honors, All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.big_th: $(bold)Big Three Dragons$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of Red, Green and White. Does not count Two Dragon Pungs, Dragon Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.four_c: $(bold)Four Concealed Pungs$()$(br)64 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Four concealed pungs (including concealed kongs). A pung completed with another player’s discard is not concealed. Does not count All Pungs, Concealed Hand. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.four_k: $(bold)Four Kongs$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Four kongs and a pair. Does not count All Pungs, Single Wait. Concealed kongs still count Concealed Kong, Two Concealed Kongs or concealed-pung patterns by number.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.four_p: $(bold)Four Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)32 points$(br2)Four chows in one suit whose starting numbers rise by one or by two. Does not count Pure Shifted Chows.
$(bold)Four Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)48 points$(br2)Four pungs in one suit, each number one higher. Does not count Pure Shifted Pungs, All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.full_f: $(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only one suit, with no honors. Does not count One Voided Suit, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.greate: $(bold)Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One of each of the seven honors plus seven tiles from 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits. Does not count Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles, All Types, Concealed Hand. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.intro: This entry lists the patterns with the highest values, in five steps of 88, 64, 48, 32 and 24 points. Most of them need the whole hand to take one shape, so they usually reach the 8-point minimum without any other pattern.
The value on each card belongs to that pattern alone and is not the total of the hand. How patterns that apply together are added is described in $(l:mcr_combining)Combining Patterns$(/l). A pattern that a card does not count is already part of that card's pattern.

For example, Thirteen Orphans is 88 points and does not count All Types, Concealed Hand or Single Wait, but adds Fully Concealed Hand (4 points) when self-drawn. A self-drawn Thirteen Orphans with no other pattern is therefore 92 points, plus flowers.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.little: $(bold)Little Four Winds$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of three winds with the fourth wind as the pair. Does not count Big Three Winds. The three wind sets do not count Pung of Terminals or Honors.
$(bold)Little Three Dragons$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of two dragons with the third dragon as the pair. Does not count Two Dragon Pungs, Dragon Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.lower_: $(bold)Lower Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only 1, 2 and 3. Does not count Lower Four, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.middle: $(bold)Middle Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only 4, 5 and 6. Does not count All Simples, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.name: 88 to 24 Points
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.nine_g: $(bold)Nine Gates$()$(br)88 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)1112345678999 of one suit, winning on any tile of that suit. Does not count Full Flush, Concealed Hand and one Pung of Terminals or Honors. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.pure_s: $(bold)Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Three pungs in one suit, each number one higher. The same tiles do not also count Pure Triple Chow.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.pure_t: $(bold)Pure Terminal Chows$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Two each of 123 and 789 in one suit, with the 5 of that suit as the pair. Does not count Full Flush, All Chows, Pure Double Chow, Two Terminal Chows, No Honors.
$(bold)Pure Triple Chow$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Three identical chows in one suit. They do not count Pure Shifted Pungs or Pure Double Chow.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.quadru: $(bold)Quadruple Chow$()$(br)48 points$(br2)Four identical chows in one suit. Does not count Pure Triple Chow, Pure Double Chow, Tile Hog.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.seven_: $(bold)Seven Pairs$()$(br)24 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Seven pairs. Four identical tiles may form two pairs and add Tile Hog. Does not count Concealed Hand, Single Wait. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.

$(bold)Seven Shifted Pairs$()$(br)88 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Seven pairs of consecutive numbers in one suit. Does not count Seven Pairs, Full Flush, Concealed Hand, Single Wait. Adds All Simples when the pairs contain no 1 or 9, and Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.thirte: $(bold)Thirteen Orphans$()$(br)88 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One of each terminal and honor plus a second copy of one as the pair. Does not count All Types, Concealed Hand, Single Wait. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.three_: $(bold)Three Kongs$()$(br)32 points$(br2)Three kongs. Concealed kongs still count Concealed Kong or Two Concealed Kongs. If all three are concealed, Three Concealed Pungs also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.upper_: $(bold)Upper Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only 7, 8 and 9. Does not count Upper Four, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.all_cho: $(bold)All Chows$()$(br)2 points$(br2)All four melds are chows and the pair is a suited tile. Does not count No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.all_sim: $(bold)All Simples$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Only 2 to 8, with no 1s, 9s or honors. Does not count No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.closed_: $(bold)Closed Wait$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The only win is the middle tile of a chow. Not counted if the hand can win another way. Only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait and Single Wait counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.conceal: $(bold)Concealed Hand$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Win on another player's discard without having called a chow, pung or melded kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. A self-drawn win with a concealed hand scores Fully Concealed Hand instead, and Concealed Hand is not counted.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.double_: $(bold)Double Pung$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Two pungs (including kongs) of the same number in different suits.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.dragon_: $(bold)Dragon Pung$()$(br)2 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of Red, Green or White.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.edge_wa: $(bold)Edge Wait$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The only win is a 3 completing 123 or a 7 completing 789. Not counted if the hand can win another way. Only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait and Single Wait counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.flower_: $(bold)Flower Tiles$()$(br)1 point per flower$(br2)Each revealed flower scores 1 point. Flower points do not count toward the 8-point minimum.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.fully_c: $(bold)Fully Concealed Hand$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Win by self-draw with a concealed hand. Concealed kongs keep the hand concealed. Does not count Concealed Hand, Self-Drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.intro: This entry lists the lowest patterns, in three steps of 4, 2 and 1 points, and flowers at 1 point each are listed here too. Most of these patterns describe only a small part of the hand, so none reaches the 8-point minimum alone and several must be added.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.intro.c: The value on each card belongs to that pattern alone and is not the total of the hand. How patterns that apply together are added is described in $(l:mcr_combining)Combining Patterns$(/l). A pattern that a card does not count is already part of that card's pattern.
For example, Fully Concealed Hand is 4 points and does not count Concealed Hand or Self-Drawn, so a closed self-drawn win earns 4 points for these three, not 4 plus 2 plus 1.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.last_ti: $(bold)Last Tile$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Win on the fourth copy of a tile when the other three are already visible. Tiles hidden in other hands or in the wall are not visible.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.melded_: $(bold)Melded Kong$()$(br)1 point$(br2)One melded kong, made on another player’s discard or by adding a tile to a melded pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.mixed_d: $(bold)Mixed Double Chow$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Two chows of the same numbers in different suits.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.name: 4 to 1 Points
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.no_hono: $(bold)No Honors$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The hand has no honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.one_voi: $(bold)One Voided Suit$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Exactly one of Characters, Circles and Bamboo is missing from the hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.outside: $(bold)Outside Hand$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a 1, a 9 or an honor.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.prevale: $(bold)Prevalent Wind$()$(br)2 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of the prevalent wind. Seat Wind also counts when it is the same wind. This set does not count Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.pung_of: $(bold)Pung of Terminals or Honors$()$(br)1 point$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of 1s or 9s, or of a wind that is neither the prevalent nor your seat wind. Dragon pungs count Dragon Pung instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.pure_do: $(bold)Pure Double Chow$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Two identical chows in one suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.seat_wi: $(bold)Seat Wind$()$(br)2 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of your seat wind. Prevalent Wind also counts when it is the same wind. This set does not count Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.self_dr: $(bold)Self-Drawn$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Win on a tile you draw yourself.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.short_s: $(bold)Short Straight$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Two chows of one suit that join into six consecutive numbers.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.single_: $(bold)Single Wait$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The only win is one tile completing the pair. Not counted if the hand can win another way. Only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait and Single Wait counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.tile_ho: $(bold)Tile Hog$()$(br)2 points$(br2)All four copies of one tile are used in the hand without forming a kong. Counts once for each such tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.two_con: $(bold)Two Concealed Pungs$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Two concealed pungs (including concealed kongs). A pung completed with another player’s discard is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.two_mel: $(bold)Two Melded Kongs$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Two melded kongs. One melded and one concealed kong score 6 points instead. In both cases Melded Kong and Concealed Kong are not counted separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.two_ter: $(bold)Two Terminal Chows$()$(br)1 point$(br2)A 123 chow and a 789 chow of the same suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.all_: $(bold)All Fives$()$(br)16 points$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a 5. Does not count All Simples, No Honors.
$(bold)All Pungs$()$(br)6 points$(br2)Four pungs (including kongs) and a pair.
$(bold)All Types$()$(br)6 points$(br2)The hand includes Characters, Circles, Bamboo, winds and dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.big_: $(bold)Big Three Winds$()$(br)12 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of three winds. They do not count Pung of Terminals or Honors, but Prevalent Wind and Seat Wind still count when they apply.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.chic: $(bold)Chicken Hand$()$(br)8 points$(br2)A win with no scoring pattern other than flowers. Flower points are added separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.half: $(bold)Half Flush$()$(br)6 points$(br2)Only one suit plus honors. Does not count One Voided Suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.intr: This entry lists the middle patterns, in four steps of 16, 12, 8 and 6 points. A pattern of 8 points or more reaches the 8-point minimum by itself, while a 6-point pattern must be added to others.

The value on each card belongs to that pattern alone and is not the total of the hand. How patterns that apply together are added is described in $(l:mcr_combining)Combining Patterns$(/l). A pattern that a card does not count is already part of that card's pattern.

For example, Last Tile Draw is 8 points and does not count Self-Drawn, so winning on the last tile of the wall earns 8 points for this pattern, not 8 plus 1 for Self-Drawn. Other patterns that apply are added as usual.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.knit: $(bold)Knitted Straight$()$(br)12 points$(br2)The nine tiles 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits, plus one meld and a pair. Only that meld may be melded. The nine tiles cannot be regrouped for other patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.last: $(bold)Last Tile Claim$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win on the discard made after another player draws the last tile of the wall.
$(bold)Last Tile Draw$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win by drawing the last tile of the wall. Does not count Self-Drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.less: $(bold)Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles$()$(br)12 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Fourteen different tiles from 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits and the honors. Does not count All Types, Concealed Hand. All nine suited tiles add Knitted Straight. A self-drawn win adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.lowe: $(bold)Lower Four$()$(br)12 points$(br2)Only 1, 2, 3 and 4. Does not count No Honors. A hand of only 1, 2 and 3 counts Lower Tiles instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.meld: $(bold)Melded Hand$()$(br)6 points$(br2)All four melds are chows, pungs or melded kongs, and the pair is completed on another player’s discard. Does not count Single Wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.mixe: $(bold)Mixed Shifted Chows$()$(br)6 points$(br2)A chow in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo whose starting numbers rise by one.
$(bold)Mixed Shifted Pungs$()$(br)8 points$(br2)A pung in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo, each number one higher.
$(bold)Mixed Straight$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Chows 123, 456 and 789, each in a different suit.
$(bold)Mixed Triple Chow$()$(br)8 points$(br2)A chow of the same numbers in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo. Mixed Double Chow is not counted among these three chows.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.name: 16 to 6 Points
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.out_: $(bold)Out with Replacement Tile$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win by drawing the replacement tile after a kong. Does not count Self-Drawn. A tile drawn to replace a flower does not count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.pure: $(bold)Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)16 points$(br2)Three chows in one suit whose starting numbers rise by one or by two.
$(bold)Pure Straight$()$(br)16 points$(br2)123, 456 and 789 of one suit. Short Straight and Two Terminal Chows are not counted among these three chows.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.reve: $(bold)Reversible Tiles$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Only tiles that look the same upside down, namely 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 of Circles, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 of Bamboo, and White. Does not count One Voided Suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.robb: $(bold)Robbing the Kong$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong. Does not count Last Tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.thre: $(bold)Three Concealed Pungs$()$(br)16 points$(br2)Three concealed pungs (including concealed kongs). A pung completed with another player’s discard counts as melded. Does not count Two Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)Three-Suited Terminal Chows$()$(br)16 points$(br2)123 and 789 in each of two suits, with a pair of 5s in the third. Does not count All Chows, Mixed Double Chow, Two Terminal Chows, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.trip: $(bold)Triple Pung$()$(br)16 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of the same number in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo. Double Pung is not counted among these three pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.two_: $(bold)Two Concealed Kongs$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Two concealed kongs. They do not count Concealed Kong or Two Concealed Pungs. A third concealed pung also counts Three Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)Two Dragon Pungs$()$(br)6 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of two dragons. They do not count Dragon Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.uppe: $(bold)Upper Four$()$(br)12 points$(br2)Only 6, 7, 8 and 9. Does not count No Honors. A hand of only 7, 8 and 9 counts Upper Tiles instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_payments.draw: A $(bold)draw$() ends a hand when the wall runs out without a win. The last discard is not won, or no tile is left to replace a flower or a kong. Nothing is paid, the deal still passes to the next player, and points already paid for false wins remain. A drawn hand counts as one of the sixteen hands.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_payments.match: A match covers the East, South, West and North rounds, four hands each, sixteen hands in all. Everyone starts at zero, and the match ends after the sixteenth hand.
The deal passes to the next player after every hand, even when the dealer wins or the hand is drawn. The dealer's seat wind is East, followed by South, West and North in turn order. The prevalent wind is East in the first round, then South, West and North. These winds decide whether $(l:mcr_fan_low#prevalent_wind)Prevalent Wind$(/l) and $(l:mcr_fan_low#seat_wind)Seat Wind$(/l) apply.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_payments.name: Payments and Rounds
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_payments.paymen: After a win, the other players pay the winner. On a self-drawn win, each of the other three players pays 8 points plus the hand value.
On a discard win, the discarder pays 8 points plus the hand value, and the other two players pay 8 points each. MCR has no dealer bonus. The table shows the payments for a hand value of 10.

Win|Who pays|Winner collects
Self-drawn|Each of the three, 18|54 in all
Discard win|Discarder 18, the other two 8 each|34 in all
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.example: Knitted Straight is 147, 258 and 369 in three suits, plus a meld and a pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.knitted: $(bold)Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles$() (12 points) is fourteen different tiles taken from 147 of one suit, 258 of another suit, 369 of the third suit and the honors, without forming melds. With all seven honors it is $(bold)Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles$() (24 points). Both need a closed hand.

A $(bold)Knitted Straight$() (12 points) is the nine tiles 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits, plus one meld and a pair. Only that meld may be called from discards. A Lesser Honors hand holding all nine suit tiles also counts the Knitted Straight.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.name: Special Hand Shapes
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.pairs: $(bold)Seven Pairs$() and $(bold)Thirteen Orphans$() are special shapes that are not divided into melds. They use the 14 tiles of your hand directly, so the hand must be closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.pairs.c: Seven Pairs (24 points) consists of seven pairs, and four identical tiles can count as two pairs. Thirteen Orphans (88 points) holds one each of the 1s and 9s of the three suits and the seven honors, plus a second copy of one of them as the pair. The cards $(l:mcr_fan_high#seven_pairs)Seven Pairs$(/l) and $(l:mcr_fan_high#thirteen_orphans)Thirteen Orphans$(/l) list what they exclude and add.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_tiles.flowers: $(bold)Flowers$() are the eight bonus tiles Plum Blossom, Orchid, Bamboo, Chrysanthemum, Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter. They have no suit and never form melds.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_tiles.flowers.c: After the deal, starting with the dealer, each player in turn reveals every flower in hand and draws a replacement for each from the back of the wall. A replacement that is a flower is replaced again.

A flower drawn during play is revealed and replaced at once. If no tile is left for the replacement, the hand is a draw.$(br2)Each flower adds 1 point to a winning hand. See $(l:mcr_winning)Winning and the Minimum$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_tiles.name: Tiles and Flowers
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_tiles.tiles: $(bold)Mahjong Competition Rules$() (MCR) is a four-player game played with 144 tiles, including 108 suit tiles, 28 honors and 8 flowers. The $(bold)suit tiles$() are Characters, Circles and Bamboo, numbered 1 to 9. The $(bold)honors$() are the winds East, South, West and North and the dragons White, Green and Red.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_tiles.tiles.con: There are four copies of every tile, and the 1s and 9s are $(bold)terminals$().$(br2)Each player is dealt 13 tiles and the dealer 14. The dealer discards first. Play goes counterclockwise. On your turn you draw a tile and discard one. Discards can be claimed. See $(l:mcr_calls)Calls and Kongs$(/l). Flowers are explained next.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.false: A $(bold)false win$() is a win declared with fewer than 8 points. The win button appears whenever the hand has a winning shape and the game does not check the points beforehand, so the button does not show that the hand reaches 8.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.false.c: The player who declares a false win at once pays each of the other three players 10 points, 30 in all, and the payment is not refunded even if another player wins later. That player cannot win for the rest of the hand but keeps drawing, discarding and calling.

After a false win on a self-drawn tile, the player still discards a tile.$(br2)When several players declare a win on one discard, every declaration below 8 points is a false win, and among the others the first in turn order after the discarder wins.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.fan: A $(bold)scoring pattern$() is a condition of the winning hand that earns points. Each pattern has a fixed value from 88 down to 1 point, and the values of the patterns that apply add up to the points of the hand.$(br2)The patterns are listed in three entries by value, namely $(l:mcr_fan_high)88 to 24 Points$(/l), $(l:mcr_fan_middle)16 to 6 Points$(/l) and $(l:mcr_fan_low)4 to 1 Points$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.fan.con: How patterns that apply together are added is described in $(l:mcr_combining)Combining Patterns$(/l).$(br2)The values follow the first edition (December 2014) of the World Mahjong Organization's Mahjong Competition Rules. Some differ from the 1998 trial rules. Two Concealed Kongs is 8 points here and 6 points in the 1998 rules.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.minimum: The $(bold)8-point minimum$() is the lowest score a hand may win with. The patterns that apply must add up to at least 8 points. Flowers do not count toward the 8. Once the hand has 8 points, each flower adds 1 more, and the total is the $(bold)hand value$().

For example, 7 points with two flowers cannot win, but 8 points with two flowers can, for a hand value of 10. The hand value decides what the other players pay. See $(l:mcr_payments)Payments and Rounds$(/l). A shape with no pattern, flowers aside, is $(l:mcr_fan_middle#chicken_hand)Chicken Hand$(/l), worth 8 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.name: Winning and the Minimum
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.shape: A $(bold)regular winning hand$() has four melds and a pair. A meld is a chow (three consecutive tiles of one suit), a pung (three identical tiles) or a kong (four identical tiles), and the pair is two identical tiles. The other shapes are in $(l:mcr_special)Special Hand Shapes$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_winning.shape.c: The tile that completes the hand is the $(bold)winning tile$(). Winning on a tile you drew is $(bold)self-drawn$(), and winning on another player's discard is a $(bold)discard win$(). The player who discarded the tile is the discarder. A win also needs 8 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.leaving: With only one human player, click the Exit button on the toolbar at any time to end the match. With several human players, the Exit button starts a vote, and the match ends only if everyone agrees. The match and its clocks pause during the vote. A missing reply does not count as agreement.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.name: Results and Replays
manual.mchjong.entry.results.replays: Click the Replays button on the toolbar or in the lobby, or type /mchjong replays in chat, to open records of matches you played. After choosing one, drag the timeline, step through or play it, jump to each decision and switch the seat you are watching.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.replays.con: Replay JSON files are exported to replays/mchjong in the game directory. Riichi mahjong replays use Tenhou format only with the default award selection. Selecting a custom award set or disabling a built-in yaku requires MChjong's native replay format. Replays of other variants also use the native format.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.settlement: After each hand, the results screen lists the outcome of the win, including the winner's yaku, fan or tai patterns, every player's score change, and han and fu in Riichi mahjong.
When several players win on one discard, you can switch between them. Click a pattern to read its explanation and open its page in this manual.$(br2)Click the Continue button when you are done. The next hand begins once everyone has confirmed.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.sticks: Ordinary mahjong tables use physical point sticks for settlement. To pay points, right-click the point-stick drawer on your side of the table to open it. Drag the required point sticks into the row for the player who should receive them.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.calls: A $(bold)call$() is taking another player's discard to complete a meld of your own. The calls are chi, pon and open kan. The meld is laid face up beside your hand and is called an $(bold)open meld$(). After a discard, each player who can claim it sees the matching buttons and Pass.
$(bold)Chi$() completes a sequence with the previous player's discard and two tiles from your hand. Only a suited tile discarded by the previous player can be claimed, since honors cannot form sequences. If the previous player discards Five of Circles, you can chi with Three and Four, Four and Six, or Six and Seven of Circles.

Chi is not allowed in three-player Riichi mahjong.$(br2)$(bold)Pon$() completes a triplet with any player's discard and two identical tiles from your hand. Claiming a discard with three identical tiles from your hand is an open kan, explained in $(l:riichi_kans)Kans$(/l). You cannot call while in riichi.

When several players claim the same tile, ron beats pon and open kan, and pon and open kan beat chi. After a chi or pon you do not draw. You discard a tile and play continues from you, so the players between the discarder and you skip their turns.

A call opens the hand. Yaku marked Closed hand only no longer count, and yaku marked Reduced by 1 han when open lose one han. Any call or kan also ends Ippatsu for every player and ends the first turn around the table, so Double Riichi, Tenhou, Chihou and Renhou are no longer possible.
The last discard, made after the last live tile has been drawn, can be claimed only for ron, not for chi, pon or kan.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.kuikae: $(bold)Kuikae$() (swap calling) is discarding, right after a chi or pon, a tile that could stand in for the claimed one. Every preset forbids it, so a call cannot be used merely to exchange one tile for an equivalent tile.

After a pon, you cannot discard a tile identical to the one you claimed. After a chi, you cannot discard a tile identical to the one you claimed, and when the claimed tile is at one end of the sequence, you also cannot discard the tile just outside the other end.
For example, after claiming Three of Characters with Four and Five, you cannot discard Three or Six of Characters. After claiming Five with Three and Four, you cannot discard Five or Two.

After claiming Four with Three and Five, only Four is forbidden. After claiming Seven with Eight and Nine, no tile exists outside the other end, so only Seven is forbidden.$(br2)You cannot call if no legal discard would remain in your hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.kuitan: Whether Tanyao still counts after calling is decided by the $(bold)kuitan$() rule. All presets count it by default. Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules can turn kuitan off, and then Tanyao counts only with a closed hand.

For example, take a hand made only of Twos to Eights with a pon of Seven of Circles. With kuitan it scores Tanyao for 1 han. Without kuitan it has no Tanyao and needs another yaku to win, as explained in $(l:riichi_yaku#tanyao)Tanyao$(/l).
A call does not require a yaku. A yaku is needed only when you win, so you may call first and build the yaku afterwards. A tenpai hand that ends up with no yaku still cannot win.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.name: Chi and Pon
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_dora.dora: A $(bold)dora indicator$() is a tile turned face up on the dead wall, and the $(bold)dora$() is the tile after it. Number tiles count up within the suit and wrap from Nine to One, winds go East, South, West, North, and dragons go White, Green, Red.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_dora.dora.co: For example, the indicator Nine of Circles makes One of Circles the dora, and the indicator North makes East the dora.$(br2)Each dora in a winning hand adds 1 han. Dora are bonuses, not yaku, so they cannot make a hand win.$(br2)There are five kinds of dora.

$(li)Dora are pointed to by the indicator revealed at the start of the hand.$(li)Kan dora are pointed to by an indicator added after a kan.$(li)Ura dora are pointed to by the hidden indicator under each revealed one, and only a player who wins after declaring riichi counts them.
$(li)Red Dora are the Red Fives of Characters, Circles and Bamboo, worth 1 han each without an indicator.$(li)North Dora are the Norths extracted in three-player Riichi mahjong, worth 1 han each.

Dora are counted in the whole winning hand, including melds, quads and the winning tile. A tile counts once for each indicator that points to it, and a tile that is both a dora and a Red Dora scores both.

For example, with the indicator Four of Bamboo every Five of Bamboo is a dora. A hand with one Red Five of Bamboo and one ordinary Five of Bamboo has 2 han for the red tile (dora plus Red Dora) and 1 han for the other, 3 han in all.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_dora.name: Dora
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_dora.presets: Which kinds of dora are used depends on the preset. Mahjong Soul, Tenhou, M.League and WRC rules use ura dora and kan dora, and JPML A rules use neither.

The number of Red Dora also depends on the preset.$(li)Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules offer none, three or four, with three as the default. Three is one red Five in each suit, and four adds a second red Five of Circles.$(li)M.League rules use three.$(li)JPML A and WRC rules use none.

When Red Dora are used, the specified number of ordinary Five of Characters, Circles or Bamboo are replaced by their red versions, so the total tile count does not change. Three-player Riichi mahjong has no Five of Characters, so only the red Fives of Circles and Bamboo exist. For the definition and counting of dora, see $(l:riichi_dora)Dora$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_draws.aborts: A hand that ends before the wall runs out because of a particular situation is an $(bold)abortive draw$(). Only the online presets (Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules) use abortive draws. The competition presets do not. Nobody wins and no no-ten penalty is paid.

The online presets have four abortive draws, and Tenhou rules in a four-player game add a fifth.$(li)$(bold)Nine terminals$() lets you abort on your first draw if no one has called and you hold nine or more different terminals and honors, by pressing the Nine Terminals button. You may also keep playing.

$(li)$(bold)Four winds$() happens when all four players discard the same wind in the first turn with no calls.$(li)$(bold)Four riichi$() happens when all four players have declared riichi.$(li)$(bold)Four kans$() happens when four kans have been made, split between two or more players.

$(li)$(bold)Triple ron$() happens when three players ron on the same discard. Only Tenhou rules in a four-player game use it, and Mahjong Soul rules let several players win.$(br2)Three-player games do not use Four winds or Four riichi.

After an abortive draw the dealer repeats, honba increases by one, and riichi sticks stay on the table for the next winner. After the fourth kan, a tsumo on the replacement tile and a ron on the next discard are resolved first, and only then is Four kans judged. If one player made all four kans, play continues.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_draws.exhaus: If the live wall runs out without a win, the hand ends as an $(bold)exhaustive draw$(). Nobody wins, so only the $(bold)no-ten penalty$() is settled. Players not in tenpai pay those in tenpai 3,000 points in total, or 2,000 in a three-player game, as the table shows.

Nothing is paid if everyone or no one is in tenpai. For example, if East and South are in tenpai and West and North are not, West and North pay 1,500 each. Who counts as tenpai is explained in Tenpai at a Draw, and three-player payments are in $(l:riichi_sanma)Three-Player Mahjong$(/l).

Afterwards the dealer repeats if in tenpai. Otherwise the next player becomes dealer. Honba increases by one either way. See $(l:riichi_rounds)Rounds and Honba$(/l). Riichi sticks stay on the table for the next winner. Players in tenpai reveal their hands.

Under the online presets, a player whose discards are all terminals and honors, none claimed, does not pay and is instead paid as for a mangan tsumo. See $(l:riichi_yaku#nagashi_mangan)Nagashi Mangan$(/l).

Tenpai|No-ten penalty
One|The other three pay 1,000 each
Two|The two others pay 1,500 each
Three|The last player pays 3,000, shared
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_draws.name: Draws
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_draws.tenpai: At an exhaustive draw, the table decides who is in tenpai from the tiles alone. This is called $(bold)formal tenpai$(), where the hand is one tile short of a winning shape. No yaku is required, furiten does not matter, and players who declared riichi and players who did not are judged the same way.

There is one exception. A wait on a tile of which all four copies are already in your own hand and melds cannot be completed, so it does not count. If every wait is like that, the hand is not in tenpai. For example, you have a pon of White Dragon, hold the fourth White Dragon in hand and need only a White Dragon for the pair.

All four are yours, so you are not in tenpai.$(br2)Tenhou rules ignore melds when judging, so the same hand still counts as tenpai. This is the only difference between Tenhou rules and the other presets in an exhaustive draw. The result decides the no-ten penalty and whether the dealer repeats.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_furiten.clea: When temporary furiten clears depends on the preset, as the table shows. A discard after a chi or pon does not follow a draw, so in the other presets, passing up a ron and then calling does not clear the furiten. Under WRC rules, your own chi, pon or open kan also clears it.

Passing a tile that cannot be won on for lack of yaku can also cause temporary furiten. Under WRC rules, passing a winning tile with a tenpai hand that has no yaku always does. In other presets it happens only when the minimum han is above one, because a hand with too little yaku cannot ron either.
Discard furiten has no timer. It clears when your hand changes so that none of the new waits is a tile you discarded. Riichi furiten never clears, because the hand cannot change after riichi.

Preset|Temporary furiten clears
Mahjong Soul, WRC|At your next draw
Other presets|When you discard after drawing
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_furiten.furi: $(bold)Furiten$() is a state caused by your own discards or by passing up a ron, and it restricts you to winning by tsumo. The rule stops a player from passing up a winning tile and then winning on another discard of it, or from waiting on a tile already thrown away.

A red Furiten label below your seat information shows the state.$(br2)There are three kinds of furiten.$(li)$(bold)Discard furiten$() applies if any of your waits is a tile you have discarded. You cannot ron on any of your waits.$(li)$(bold)Temporary furiten$() applies after you pass up a ron.

You cannot ron until it clears.$(li)$(bold)Riichi furiten$() applies after you pass up a ron following riichi. It lasts for the rest of the hand.$(br2)Discard furiten is judged on your own river. Discards that other players claimed, discards made before you were in tenpai and the riichi declaration tile all count.

For example, you wait on Two and Five of Circles and discarded a Five earlier. You cannot ron on a Two either, only win by tsumo. Choosing a call instead of ron, or running out of time, also counts as passing up a ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_furiten.name: Furiten
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_kans.after: After declaring a kan, you draw a $(bold)replacement tile$() from the dead wall and then discard a tile. Winning by tsumo on that tile is $(l:riichi_yaku#rinshan_kaihou)Rinshan Kaihou$(/l). After an open kan, the kan player continues the turn.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_kans.after.c: The dead wall has four replacement tiles in four-player Riichi mahjong and eight in three-player Riichi mahjong, where kans and North extractions share them. When none is left, no more kans can be declared.$(br2)A preset with kan dora reveals one more dora indicator after each kan. See $(l:riichi_dora)Dora$(/l).

A concealed kan reveals it at once. Under Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules, an open or added kan reveals it only after the kan player discards, so a Rinshan Kaihou win after an open kan does not count it. M.League and WRC rules reveal it at once for every kan. JPML A rules have no kan dora.

When another player adds a kan to a triplet, a player who qualifies for ron can win on the tile being added. This is $(bold)robbing the kan$(). See $(l:riichi_yaku#chankan)Chankan$(/l). Passing it up causes furiten like any passed ron. Mahjong Soul rules also allow robbing a concealed kan, but only for Kokushi Musou. After riichi only a concealed kan is possible. See $(l:riichi_riichi)Riichi$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_kans.kans: A $(bold)kan$() turns four identical tiles into a quad, which counts as one meld. There are three kinds of kan, and open and added kans are together called exposed kans. A quad earns extra fu. See $(l:riichi_points)Fu and Scoring$(/l). A preset with kan dora also reveals another dora indicator for every player.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_kans.kans.co: See $(l:riichi_dora)Dora$(/l).$(br2)The three kinds differ in where the tiles come from.$(li)A $(bold)concealed kan$() uses four identical tiles from your hand. The hand stays closed.$(li)An $(bold)open kan$() uses a discard and three identical tiles from your hand.

The hand opens.$(li)An $(bold)added kan$() adds the fourth tile to a triplet made earlier by pon.$(br2)For example, holding three Five of Bamboo and drawing the fourth allows a concealed kan. Holding three when another player discards the fourth allows an open kan.

After a pon of Five of Bamboo, drawing the fourth allows an added kan. All three are the Kan button.$(br2)A kan needs a replacement tile from the dead wall, and the whole table can make at most four kans in one hand. Kans after riichi are restricted. See $(l:riichi_riichi)Riichi$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_kans.name: Kans
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.fu: $(bold)Fu$() is the second scoring number of a winning hand. Han is the total of its yaku and dora, while fu comes from the shape of the hand. Every hand starts at 20 fu and adds the items in the table.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.fu.co: Triplets and quads of terminals and honors are worth double the values for tiles two to eight. A triplet completed by ron counts as open. A pair that is both the round wind and your seat wind is 4 fu under Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules and 2 fu under M.League, JPML A and WRC rules.

manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.fu_to: The total is rounded up to a multiple of 10. Pinfu tsumo is fixed at 20 fu without the tsumo bonus, and Chiitoitsu is fixed at 25 fu without rounding. An open hand with nothing beyond the base 20 fu counts as 30 fu.

For example, a closed hand wins by ron on an edge wait with a concealed triplet of Red Dragon, so it has 20 + 10 + 8 + 2 = 40 fu. Another closed hand wins by tsumo on a closed wait with a concealed triplet of 3 Bamboo, so it has 20 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 28 fu, rounded up to 30 fu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.limit: A hand whose base points reach 2,000 stops growing and is paid from the fixed base points in the table. Five han, or fewer han with enough fu to reach 2,000 base points (such as 4 han 40 fu or 3 han 70 fu), is a mangan.

M.League and WRC rules use kiriage mangan, which also pays 4 han 30 fu and 3 han 60 fu as mangan. M.League rules have no counted yakuman and score sanbaiman at most for 13 han or more, while the other presets pay one yakuman. See $(l:riichi_yakuman)Yakuman$(/l) for the yakuman hands.

Payments work as below mangan. In a mangan with 2,000 base points, a nondealer ron pays 8,000 and a dealer ron pays 12,000. A nondealer tsumo is 4,000 from the dealer and 2,000 from each other player, and a dealer tsumo is 4,000 from each player.

manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.name: Fu and Scoring
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.point: A hand below mangan starts from its $(bold)base points$(), which are fu × 2^(han + 2). Han is the total of yaku and dora, and fu is explained in Fu. For example, a nondealer with 3 han 40 fu has 40 × 2^5 = 1,280 base points.$(br2)The base points times the multiples in the table give the payments.

On a ron the discarder pays alone, and on a tsumo every other player pays. Every payment is rounded up to 100 points separately. In the example, a nondealer ron is 1,280 × 4 = 5,120, rounded up to 5,200. On a nondealer tsumo, the dealer pays 2,560, up to 2,600, and each other player 1,280, up to 1,300.

A dealer ron is 1,280 × 6 = 7,680, rounded up to 7,700.$(br2)A nondealer with two-han Chiitoitsu has 25 fu, so 25 × 2^4 = 400 base points and a ron pays 1,600. The winner also takes the riichi sticks on the table, plus 300 points per honba. See $(l:riichi_rounds)Rounds and Honba$(/l).

manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.choi: Riichi mahjong has seven $(bold)rule presets$(). Mahjong Soul rules and Tenhou rules each come for four players and for three, and M.League, JPML A and WRC rules are for four players only.

This chapter calls Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules the $(bold)online presets$(), after the online games they imitate, and M.League, JPML A and WRC rules the $(bold)competition presets$(), after the tournament rules they follow.

The online presets let you change whether All Simples counts with calls (kuitan), the number of Red Fives, the minimum han a winning hand needs and the match length. Changing any other rule, or any rule of a competition preset, adds (Custom) to the preset name.
The presets differ in how final results are scored from points, how a match proceeds and ends, and who is liable for a yakuman. The sections of this chapter take them in that order.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.comp: The competition presets (M.League, JPML A and WRC rules) play the way tournaments do. They use no bankruptcy, abortive draws, Nagashi Mangan, agari yame or extra rounds. If the dealer repeats in the last hand, play continues until the dealer no longer repeats.
When several players ron on one tile, only the first of them in turn order after the discarder wins, and the other rons do not count. This is called $(bold)head bump$().

M.League rules use three Red Fives, and JPML A and WRC rules use none. Riichi sticks left on the table at the end of the match go to first place under M.League rules and stay undistributed under JPML A and WRC rules. JPML A rules have no Ippatsu, ura dora or kan dora, and WRC rules use Blessing of Man, scored as a mangan.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.floa: Under JPML A rules the uma is not fixed. It depends on the $(bold)floating count$(), the number of players who finish with 30,000 points or more, that is, at least the return. The table gives the uma for first to fourth place at each floating count.

For example, final points of 42,000, 31,000, 25,000 and 22,000 give a floating count of 2. The results are (42,000 - 30,000) / 1,000 + 8 = 20, then 1 + 4 = 5, -5 - 4 = -9 and -8 - 8 = -16, which sum to zero.$(br2)How players with equal final points are ranked depends on the preset.

Under the competition presets, tied players share the uma and oka of the places they occupy, and M.League rules distribute leftover hundreds from the first dealer onward. The online presets break ties by seat order from the first dealer, so the player closer to the first dealer ranks higher.

manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.name: Rule Presets
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.onli: The online presets (Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules) end a match in the way online games do.$(br2)The match ends at once when any player's points fall below zero, which is called $(bold)bankruptcy$(). Exactly zero continues.

In the last hand, if the dealer would repeat while in first place with at least the target score, the match ends instead. It is $(bold)agari yame$() when the dealer repeats by winning and $(bold)tenpai yame$() when the dealer repeats by being in tenpai at a draw. The target score is 30,000 for four players and 40,000 for three.
If first place is below the target score when the last hand ends, an $(bold)extra round$() begins. It ends with the hand in which someone reaches the target score, for at most one round.

When several players ron on one discard, Mahjong Soul rules let them all win, while under Tenhou rules a triple ron is a draw. See $(l:riichi_draws)Draws$(/l). Riichi sticks left on the table at the end go to first place.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.pao: When a player enables another player's yakuman, that player must pay for it. This is called $(bold)liability$() (pao). It covers Daisangen (three sets of dragon tiles) and Daisuushii (four sets of wind tiles).
If your discard lets another player pon or open-kan their third dragon set or fourth wind set, you are liable for that Daisangen or Daisuushii. The competition presets also apply liability to a fourth kan completed by an open kan, which is Suukantsu.

If the winner wins by tsumo, the liable player pays that yakuman in full. If a third player deals in, the liable player and the discarder pay half each. For example, your Green Dragon lets another player pon their third dragon set.

That nondealer later wins Daisangen by ron on a third player's discard, so the 32,000 points are split and you and the discarder pay 16,000 each.$(br2)Under Tenhou rules, when a liable yakuman combines with another yakuman, the whole hand is settled as liable.

Other presets make the liable player pay only the liable part. Under JPML A and WRC rules the discarder pays the honba in liability cases, and under WRC rules on a tsumo with a yakuman beyond the liable one, every player pays the honba.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.scor: When a match ends, each player's result is (final points - return) / 1,000 plus the uma for that placement. The $(bold)return$() is the reference score, the $(bold)uma$() is a bonus or penalty set by placement, and the $(bold)oka$(), the return minus the starting points times the number of players, goes to first place.

For example, under Tenhou rules with four players, final points of 38,000, 27,000, 22,000 and 13,000 give first place (38,000 - 30,000) / 1,000 + 20 + 20 = 48, and fourth place (13,000 - 30,000) / 1,000 - 20 = -37.
Under Mahjong Soul rules, four players start with 25,000 and return 25,000, so there is no oka, with uma +15/+5/-5/-15. Three players start with 35,000 and return 35,000, with uma +15/0/-15.
Under Tenhou rules, four players start with 25,000 and return 30,000, with uma +20/+10/-10/-20. Three players start with 35,000 and return 40,000, with uma +20/0/-20.

The three competition presets also score a result as (final points - return) / 1,000 plus the uma, as explained in the previous section. Under M.League rules players start with 25,000 and return 30,000, so first place also gets an oka of 20, with uma +30/+10/-10/-30.

Under WRC rules players start and return 30,000, so there is no oka, with uma +15/+5/-5/-15. Under JPML A rules players start and return 30,000 with no oka, and the uma depends on how many players finish with at least 30,000 points. See $(l:riichi_presets#floating)JPML A Placement Bonuses$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_riichi.after: After riichi the hand is locked. You discard every tile you draw, except when you win, declare a concealed kan or extract North. You cannot chi, pon or call an open or added kan, and you cannot choose a different tile to discard. If another player discards a tile you wait on, you can only ron or pass.
A concealed kan after riichi must not change the waits. You must have drawn the fourth tile yourself, and the waits after the kan must be exactly the waits before it.

For example, a hand with three Three of Bamboo, one Four of Bamboo and three other complete melds waits on Two, Four and Five of Bamboo. Drawing the fourth Three of Bamboo and declaring a kan would leave only Four of Bamboo, so it is not allowed.

M.League, JPML A and WRC rules also forbid changing the hand's meld composition. However the tenpai hand is read, the three tiles must form a triplet. JPML A rules additionally forbid losing an existing yaku. Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules only require the waits to stay the same.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_riichi.depos: The deposits on the table all go to the next player who wins, including those left by earlier hands that ended in a draw. If several players ron on one discard, the deposits and the honba go to the first of them in turn order after the discarder.

After a draw, the deposits stay on the table for the next hand. Nagashi Mangan does not take them.$(br2)For example, with three deposits on the table, a nondealer who wins by ron receives 3,000 points in addition to the points of the win. The honba and deposit counts shown at the table change accordingly.

What happens to deposits left at the end of the match depends on the preset. Mahjong Soul, Tenhou and M.League rules give them to the player in first place. JPML A and WRC rules do not distribute them. Placement and final scores are covered in $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_riichi.name: Riichi
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_riichi.riich: $(bold)Riichi$() is a declaration, made with a closed hand in tenpai, by discarding a tile and paying 1,000 points. The 1,000 points go onto the table as a $(bold)deposit$() and stay there until a player wins. Riichi is also a one-han yaku, see $(l:riichi_yaku#riichi)Riichi$(/l), and it opens the chance of Ippatsu and ura dora.

Three conditions must hold. The hand is closed, which a concealed kan does not change. The hand is in tenpai after the chosen discard. And your points and the tiles left in the wall meet the preset, as the table shows.

Press Riichi, then click one of the highlighted tiles. Only discards that keep the hand in tenpai are highlighted. Right-click or Esc cancels. The tile is discarded sideways. If another player rons on this discard, the riichi does not take effect and no deposit is paid.
Otherwise the 1,000 points are paid, even if another player claims the tile with chi or pon. With 25,000 points, riichi leaves you with 24,000 and adds one deposit to the table.

manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_rounds.deale: The $(bold)dealer$() is the player holding East for the hand, and the other players are $(bold)nondealers$(). The dealer wins and loses more points in a hand, so who deals changes with the result, as the table shows. An exhaustive draw is explained in $(l:riichi_draws)Draws$(/l).

When several players ron on one discard and the dealer is among them, the dealer repeats. When the dealer repeats, seats and seat winds stay as they were. When the deal moves on, each player's seat wind moves one step.
For example, in South 2 the dealer is the player who started at West. If that player is not in tenpai at an exhaustive draw, the player after them deals South 3, and the honba count rises by one.

manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_rounds.honba: $(bold)Honba$() counts dealer repeats and draws, and it adds extra points to a win. A dealer repeat or a draw adds one honba, and a nondealer win resets the count to zero. A dealer win that repeats also adds one. The table shows the extra points the winner receives for each honba.

For example, with two honba, a nondealer who wins by ron receives 600 points from the discarder on top of the hand's value, and a tsumo adds 200 points from each other player. When several players ron on one discard, only the first of them receives the honba.
The honba count and the deposits are both shown at the table. Deposits are the 1,000-point riichi payments and go to the next winner. See $(l:riichi_riichi)Riichi$(/l). They are not honba.
