manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_rounds.name: Rounds and Honba
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_rounds.round: A match is made of hands. By default it is a $(bold)hanchan$(), an East round followed by a South round.

In each round every seat deals in turn, so a round has four hands in four-player Riichi mahjong and three in three-player Riichi mahjong, and a hanchan is scheduled for 8 hands (6 in three-player games). A dealer repeat adds hands beyond the schedule.

Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules can shorten the match to a $(bold)tonpuusen$(), an East round only.$(br2)A hand name such as East 2, 1 honba gives the round wind, which dealer turn of the round it is, and the honba count. The first dealer sits at East, and the deal then passes counterclockwise.

Endings such as bankruptcy, agari yame and extra rounds depend on the preset. See $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l). Competition presets end after the scheduled hands, but continue if the dealer repeats in the last hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.name: Three-Player Mahjong
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.north: In a three-player game a North tile can stay in your hand as an ordinary tile, or you can $(bold)extract North$() by setting it aside in front of you and drawing a replacement from the dead wall. You do this on your own turn. It is not a kan, and chi and pon do not apply.
The replacement tile is treated like a draw, so you may extract again, declare riichi or win with it. Each extracted North adds one han of North Dora, plus its own dora value if North itself is dora. Extracting keeps the hand closed but breaks Ippatsu for every player. After riichi you may extract only the North you just drew.

A tsumo on the replacement tile also scores Rinshan Kaihou. The first four replacement draws, kans included, come from the dead wall. Further ones are taken from the end of the live wall, which shortens it.

When another player extracts North, a player waiting on North who meets the ron conditions can ron on it. This is called robbing North and does not score Chankan. A player in furiten cannot ron on it.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.paymen: Three-player points follow the four-player scoring, with one payer fewer. On a tsumo, the other two players pay the amounts their dealer or nondealer roles would pay in a four-player game, and nobody covers the absent fourth player's share.

For example, a nondealer mangan tsumo collects 4,000 from the dealer and 2,000 from the other nondealer. A dealer mangan tsumo collects 4,000 from each, 8,000 in all. A ron pays as in four-player games, which is 8,000 for a nondealer mangan and 12,000 for a dealer mangan.

After an exhaustive draw the no-ten penalty totals 2,000 points. With one player in tenpai, the other two pay 1,000 each. With two in tenpai, the third pays 2,000, shared between them. Nothing is paid if all or none are in tenpai.

Each honba adds 200 points to a ron, paid by the discarder, and 100 points from each of the other two players to a tsumo. Three-player games have no Four winds or Four riichi abortive draws. See $(l:riichi_draws)Draws$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.tiles: $(bold)Three-player mahjong$() is Riichi mahjong for three players. Both Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules have a three-player preset. The 2 to 8 of Characters are removed, leaving the 1 and 9 of Characters and 108 tiles in all, so Characters cannot form sequences.
Chi is not allowed. Only pon and kan.$(br2)The three players sit East, South and West. A round ends after each of them has been dealer once, so there are three dealer turns per round. Each player is dealt 13 tiles and the dealer 14.
Dora indicators work slightly differently. When the 1 of Characters is the indicator, the dora is the 9 of Characters, and the other way round. Every other indicator points to the next tile as usual.
Players start with 35,000 points. At the end of the match the return is 35,000 under Mahjong Soul rules and 40,000 under Tenhou rules. See $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_tiles.name: Tiles and the Wall
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_tiles.play: At the start of a hand each player is dealt 13 tiles, the $(bold)starting hand$(), and the dealer draws a 14th tile as the first draw. The dealer's seat wind is East. Going counterclockwise, the other players have South, West and North. Seat winds move on whenever the dealer changes.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_tiles.play.c: Play goes counterclockwise, beginning with the dealer. On your turn you draw one tile from the wall and then discard one, which brings your hand back to its size before the draw. The discard is placed face up in your $(bold)river$(), the row of your discards in front of you, and cannot be taken back.

Discarding the tile you just drew is $(bold)tsumogiri$(). Discarding a tile that was already in your hand is $(bold)tedashi$().$(br2)After each discard the other players may win by ron, claim the tile with pon, kan or chi, or pass. See $(l:riichi_calls)Chi and Pon$(/l).

If nobody reacts, the player after the discarder draws next. When a player claims the tile, that player discards next, and the players between the discarder and the claimer skip their draws.$(br2)The table lists the actions you can take at that moment, such as Tsumo, Riichi, Kan and Pass.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_tiles.tiles: Four-player Riichi mahjong is played with 136 tiles. The $(bold)suited tiles$() are the suits Characters, Circles and Bamboo, numbered One to Nine with four copies of each number, 108 tiles in all.
The $(bold)honors$() are the four winds, East, South, West and North, and the three dragons, White, Green and Red, four copies each, 28 tiles in all. There are no flowers.$(br2)The Ones and Nines are $(bold)terminals$(). Terminals and honors together are $(bold)terminal and honor tiles$(), and the Twos to Eights are $(bold)simples$().

Yaku such as Tanyao and Honroutou are judged by these groups. See $(l:riichi_yaku)Yaku$(/l).$(br2)There are only four copies of each tile. When you can see all four of a tile, in your hand, in rivers and in melds, nobody can draw or discard it any more. Honors cannot form sequences, only pairs and triplets. See $(l:riichi_winning)Winning and Tenpai$(/l).

Some of the Fives can be red. A Red Five is an ordinary Five that is also a Red Dora. See $(l:riichi_dora)Dora$(/l). Three-player Riichi mahjong removes the Twos to Eights of Characters and uses 108 tiles. See $(l:riichi_sanma)Three-Player Mahjong$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_tiles.wall: The $(bold)wall$() is the stack of shuffled tiles that players draw from. A roll of two dice at the start of each hand decides where it is opened. The last 14 tiles are the $(bold)dead wall$(), and the tiles before it are the $(bold)live wall$(), from which players draw one tile per turn.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_tiles.wall.c: The dead wall holds the dora indicators and the replacement tiles drawn after a kan. Every replacement draw moves one tile from the end of the live wall into the dead wall, so the dead wall stays at 14 tiles and the live wall becomes one tile shorter.

The deal takes 52 tiles, so a four-player live wall holds 70 tiles after the deal. Without calls or kans they are drawn in turn order, and the player after the dealer draws the last one. A tsumo on that tile is $(l:riichi_yaku#haitei_raoyue)Haitei Raoyue$(/l), a ron on the last discard is $(l:riichi_yaku#houtei_raoyui)Houtei Raoyui$(/l), and the last discard cannot be claimed with chi, pon or kan.
If the live wall has run out and nobody has won, the hand is an exhaustive draw. Players not in tenpai pay those in tenpai, and the dealer repeats when in tenpai. See $(l:riichi_draws)Draws$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_winning.name: Winning and Tenpai
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_winning.requ: A win needs at least one han from yaku. This is the $(bold)minimum han$() and it is one han by default. Dora add han but are not yaku, so a hand with nothing but dora cannot win. Yakuman ignore the minimum.

Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules can raise the minimum to two or four han. Only the han of yaku are counted. Riichi plus Menzen Tsumo is 2 han and meets a two-han minimum, while Riichi with four dora has only 1 han of yaku and cannot win. M.League, JPML A and WRC rules always use one han.

Under Tenhou rules, Ippatsu does not count toward the minimum. Under Mahjong Soul rules it does. When a complete hand lacks enough yaku, the Tsumo and Ron buttons do not appear. With a minimum above one han, passing such a tile also causes furiten. See $(l:riichi_furiten)Furiten$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_winning.shap: A $(bold)winning shape$() is the arrangement a hand must have to win. The standard winning shape is four melds and one pair. A $(bold)meld$() is a sequence, a triplet or a quad. A $(bold)sequence$() is three consecutive numbers of one suit, such as Two, Three and Four of Circles. A $(bold)triplet$() is three identical tiles.

A $(bold)quad$() is four identical tiles declared as a kan. A $(bold)pair$() is two identical tiles.$(br2)Honors cannot form sequences, only pairs, triplets and quads. A winning hand has 14 tiles when it has no quad, and each quad adds one tile. The total includes melds laid out after a chi, pon or kan.

$(l:riichi_yaku#chiitoitsu)Chiitoitsu$(/l) and $(l:riichi_yakuman#kokushi_musou)Kokushi Musou$(/l) use different winning shapes.$(br2)For example, 123 of Characters, 456 of Bamboo, three Red Dragons, a pair of East and 34 of Circles make three melds, a pair and a two-tile partial sequence. Drawing Two or Five of Circles turns it into four melds and a pair, 14 tiles in all.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_winning.tenp: A hand with no chi, pon or open kan, that is, with no meld made from another player's tile, is a $(bold)closed hand$(). A concealed kan keeps the hand closed. Yaku marked Closed hand only can score only in this state, and riichi requires it. See $(l:riichi_riichi)Riichi$(/l).
A hand is in $(bold)tenpai$() when one more tile would complete a winning shape. Those tiles are its $(bold)waits$(). Tenpai depends only on the shape and does not require a yaku.

For example, the 13 tiles 123 of Characters, 456 of Bamboo, three Red Dragons, a pair of East and 34 of Circles are in tenpai, and the waits are Two and Five of Circles. When the wall runs out, players in tenpai also receive points from those who are not. See $(l:riichi_draws)Draws$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_winning.win: $(bold)Tsumo$() is winning on a tile you drew yourself, and $(bold)ron$() is winning on a tile another player discarded. That player is the $(bold)discarder$(). The Tsumo and Ron buttons appear only when the win is legal. The hand must have a winning shape and a yaku, and for a ron you must not be in furiten.
Winning is not compulsory. Passing up a ron is called $(bold)minogashi$(). For example, you wait on Two and Five of Circles and another player discards a Five. If you pass, you cannot ron on Two or Five of Circles until the furiten clears, although you can still win by tsumo. See $(l:riichi_furiten)Furiten$(/l).

Several players can ron on the same discard. Whether all of them win depends on the preset. Under M.League, JPML A and WRC rules only the first of them in turn order after the discarder wins, which is called head bump. See $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l). A win ends the hand, and the points are settled as described in $(l:riichi_points)Fu and Scoring$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chankan: $(bold)Chankan$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by ron on the fourth tile another player adds to an exposed triplet.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chanta: $(bold)Chanta$()$(br)2 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a terminal or honor, with at least one sequence and at least one honor.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chiitoi: $(bold)Chiitoitsu$()$(br)2 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Seven different pairs. Four identical tiles cannot be two pairs.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chinits: $(bold)Chinitsu$()$(br)6 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Only one suit with no honors. Chinitsu supersedes Honitsu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.double_: $(bold)Double Riichi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Declare riichi on your first discard before anyone has called, then win. Double Riichi supersedes Riichi.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.haitei_: $(bold)Haitei Raoyue$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by tsumo on the last normally drawable tile of the wall. Replacement tiles are not the last tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.honitsu: $(bold)Honitsu$()$(br)3 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Only one suit plus honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.honrout: $(bold)Honroutou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Only terminals and honors. With four melds and a pair, Toitoi also counts. In the seven-pairs shape, Chiitoitsu also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.houtei_: $(bold)Houtei Raoyui$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Ron on the discard made after the last tile is drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.iipeiko: $(bold)Iipeikou$()$(br)1 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Two identical sequences of the same suit and numbers.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.intro: A $(bold)yaku$() is a condition a hand must satisfy to win. Even a complete hand cannot win without at least one yaku, which is called yaku-less.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.intro.c: $(l:riichi_dora)Dora$(/l) are not yaku and only add han. Each yaku has its own $(bold)han$() value. A hand's total is the han of all its yaku plus its dora, and $(l:riichi_points)Fu and Scoring$(/l) turns the total into points.

This chapter lists the regular yaku. The value under each name is that yaku's own han. Yaku marked "Reduced by 1 han when open" lose one han with calls, and yaku marked "Closed hand only" do not count with calls. Yakuman have their own chapter, $(l:riichi_yakuman)Yakuman$(/l).
The online presets can raise the minimum han to 2 or 4. Then the han of the yaku alone, without dora, must reach the minimum before the hand can win. Tenhou rules do not count Ippatsu toward it.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.ippatsu: $(bold)Ippatsu$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win after riichi before your next discard, with no chi, pon, kan or North extraction by anyone in between. JPML A rules do not use Ippatsu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.ittsu: $(bold)Ittsu$()$(br)2 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Sequences 123, 456 and 789 of one suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.junchan: $(bold)Junchan$()$(br)3 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a 1 or 9, with at least one sequence and no honors. Junchan supersedes Chanta.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.menzen_: $(bold)Menzen Tsumo$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by tsumo with a closed hand. Concealed kans keep the hand closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.nagashi: $(bold)Nagashi Mangan$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules only. At an exhaustive draw, all your discards are terminals or honors and none was called.
Mahjong Soul rules also require no calls of your own. Tenhou rules allow them. Paid as a mangan tsumo instead of noten payments, without honba or riichi sticks.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.name: Yaku
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.pinhu: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)1 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)All four melds are sequences, the pair is not yakuhai, and the hand wins on a two-sided wait. It also counts by tsumo.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.renhou: $(bold)Blessing of Man$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)WRC rules only. A nondealer wins by ron before their first draw, with no calls by anyone. The higher of mangan and the normal score counts. Scored as mangan, it counts no other yaku or dora.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.riichi: $(bold)Riichi$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Declare riichi with a closed hand in tenpai by discarding a tile and depositing 1,000 points, then win.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.rinshan: $(bold)Rinshan Kaihou$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by tsumo on the replacement tile after a kan. In three-player Riichi mahjong, a tsumo on the replacement after North extraction also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.ryanpei: $(bold)Ryanpeikou$()$(br)3 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Two Iipeikou plus a pair. Ryanpeikou supersedes Iipeikou and Chiitoitsu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.sananko: $(bold)Sanankou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Three concealed triplets (including concealed quads). A triplet completed by ron is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.sanshok: $(bold)Sanshoku Doujun$()$(br)2 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)A sequence with the same numbers in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo.
$(bold)Sanshoku Doukou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)A triplet (including quads) with the same number in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.shousan: $(bold)Shousangen$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of two dragons with the third dragon as the pair. The two dragon sets also score yakuhai, so the hand has at least 4 han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.tanyao: $(bold)Tanyao$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Only tiles from 2 to 8. Whether it counts after calls is explained under $(l:riichi_calls#kuitan)Kuitan$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.toitoi: $(bold)Toitoi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)All four melds are triplets (including quads).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.yakuhai: $(bold)Yakuhai$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of the round wind, your seat wind or a dragon (White, Green or Red), each worth 1 han. A tile that is both the round and seat wind counts both, for 2 han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.chih: $(bold)Chiihou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)A nondealer wins by tsumo on their first draw before anyone has called.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.chin: $(bold)Chinroutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only 1s and 9s, with all four melds triplets (including quads).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.chuu: $(bold)Pure Chuuren Poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Before the win, the hand is exactly one suit’s 1112345678999 and can win on any tile from 1 to 9 of that suit. Pure Chuuren Poutou supersedes Chuuren Poutou.
$(bold)Chuuren Poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One suit’s 1112345678999 plus any other tile of that suit. Kans are not allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.dais: $(bold)Daisangen$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of White, Green and Red.
$(bold)Daisuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of East, South, West and North.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.intr: A $(bold)yakuman$() is the highest-valued yaku. It is paid without counting fu, with 32,000 points for a nondealer ron and 48,000 for a dealer ron. The tsumo payments are in $(l:riichi_points)Fu and Scoring$(/l). Yakuman do not add regular yaku or dora. A counted yakuman from 13 or more han is paid the same amount.

When one hand has several yakuman, their values add up, which every preset allows. Mahjong Soul rules count Kokushi Musou Thirteen-Sided Wait, Suuankou Tanki, Pure Chuuren Poutou and Daisuushii as double yakuman, worth two yakuman by themselves. Other rules count them once.
Daisangen, Daisuushii and, under the competition presets, Suukantsu carry liability, so the player who enabled the yakuman pays for the winner. See $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.koku: $(bold)Kokushi Musou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One of each of the thirteen terminals and honors, with a second copy of one of them as the pair.

$(bold)Kokushi Musou Thirteen-Sided Wait$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Before the win, the hand holds one of each of the thirteen terminals and honors and can win on any of them. Kokushi Musou Thirteen-Sided Wait supersedes Kokushi Musou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.name: Yakuman
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.ryuu: $(bold)Ryuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 of Bamboo and the Green Dragon. The Green Dragon is not required.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.shou: $(bold)Shousuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of three winds with the fourth wind as the pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.suua: $(bold)Suuankou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Four concealed triplets (including concealed quads). With a dual-pon wait it counts only by tsumo, because a triplet completed by ron is not concealed.
$(bold)Suuankou Tanki$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four concealed triplets (including quads) are complete, and the hand wins on a single wait for the pair. Ron also counts. Suuankou Tanki supersedes Suuankou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.suuk: $(bold)Suukantsu$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four quads and a pair, open or concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.tenh: $(bold)Tenhou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)The dealer wins with the dealt hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.tsuu: $(bold)Tsuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only honors, and the seven-pairs shape also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.invite: The host can click the Invite Player button in the lobby sidebar or type /mchjong invite <player> in chat. Invitations expire after 60 seconds. Without invitation teleporting, approach within six blocks of the table's center before accepting. Acceptance seats you directly when a seat is available.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.invite.cont: With invitation teleporting enabled, you can accept from farther away. After arriving beside the table, sit down to join.$(br2)Computer players can fill empty seats. Riichi mahjong offers Easy and Hard computer players. MCR, Sichuan mahjong and Taiwanese mahjong each offer one difficulty level.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.lobby: Right-click an empty mahjong stool to sit down. The first player seated becomes the host. Sitting down opens the table’s lobby.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.lobby.conti: The host chooses the variant in the lobby sidebar and selects a rule preset, the number of players and other rules under the Match Settings option. Hover over a rule to read its description. Changing the rules clears every player’s ready status.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.name: Starting a Match
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.start: When every seat is filled, the host clicks the Assign Seats and Continue or Draw Winds and Continue button. An automatic table assigns seats directly. At an ordinary table, each player draws a face-down wind tile to decide the seats.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.start.conti: Each player then sits in the assigned seat and clicks the Ready button. The Automatic Reseating option, on by default, moves you to your seat. The match starts when everyone is ready and the equipment meets the selected rules. The Table Preparation screen lists anything missing.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_dealer.deal: A $(bold)match$() consists of several hands, and a hand runs from the shuffle and deal until it ends by wins or a draw.

Both presets play eight hands, and the host can set 1 to 64 in the rule settings. When the last hand is over, players are ranked by total points, which include win payments, kong payments, ready checks and flower-pig deductions.

Each hand has one $(bold)dealer$(), who is dealt 14 tiles and discards first. The other three players are dealt 13. Sichuan mahjong has no dealer bonus or multiplier.$(br2)The player who wins first in a hand deals the next hand. If that first win is several players winning on the same discard, the discarder deals.

If nobody wins, the dealer stays. Every hand is shuffled, dealt and voided anew.$(br2)For example, A deals, B wins first and C then wins by self-draw, so B deals next. If B and C instead win together on A's discard, A deals again.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_dealer.name: Dealers and Hands
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_draws.draws: A $(bold)draw$() ends a hand when the wall runs out with fewer than three players having won. Once the last tile has been drawn and the discard after it is settled, the players who have not won are classified as ready or not ready, make the ready check and refund kong points.

A hand is $(bold)ready$() when one more tile of a suit other than its void suit would complete a winning shape. Tiles seen in the discards do not matter. It only counts that your own hand and called tiles do not already hold all four copies. A hand that still holds void-suit tiles is never ready.

In the $(bold)ready check$(), each player who is not ready pays every ready player the highest base points that player's hand could reach, after the fan cap. Fan that depend on the timing of the win, such as Win After Kong, Win on a Discard After a Kong, Robbing the Kong and Last-Tile Win, are not counted, and neither is the self-draw bonus.

A player who is not ready also refunds the kong points collected earlier, each to the player who paid it, except points already transferred by call transfer. Both presets refund, and the rule settings can switch it off.

For example, A has won and left. D made a concealed kong earlier and collected 2 points each from B and C. At the draw, B is ready for at most 2 base points, C for 8, and D is not ready. D pays B 2 and C 8 and refunds 2 kong points to each, ending at -10, with B at +2 and C at +8.
A hand that ends with three winners has no ready check and no refund.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_draws.flowe: A $(bold)flower pig$() is a player who breaks the void-suit rule, and there are two kinds with different results. The void-suit rule is in $(l:sichuan_void)Void Suits$(/l).

A $(bold)passive flower pig$() is a player who still holds void-suit tiles when the hand ends in a draw. The player is treated as not ready, so pays every ready player in the ready check and refunds kong points, but loses no further points.

An $(bold)active flower pig$() is a player who breaks the void-suit rule during play, either by calling or konging a void-suit tile, or by discarding a tile of another suit while still holding void-suit tiles, not counting the tile just drawn.

An active flower pig loses 24 competition points at once, which are paid to no one, and the amount can be changed in the rule settings. The player can no longer win, refunds all kong points collected so far to the players who paid them, and collects no kong points afterwards.
In a draw, an active flower pig collects nothing in the ready check. If the player's hand is not ready, the player still pays the ready players. If it is ready, the player pays nothing.

For example, A has made a concealed kong and collected 6 points. A is ruled an active flower pig, loses 24 points at once and refunds the 6 points, 2 to each of B, C and D. A ends at -24, B, C and D at 0 each, and the 24 deducted points go to no one.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_draws.name: Draws and Checks
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.all_pun: $(bold)All Pungs$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Four pungs (including kongs) and a pair. Seven pairs does not count All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.base: $(bold)Base points$() depend on the fan and are 2 to the power of the fan, as the table shows. The fan of a hand is the sum of the values of its scoring patterns, which the following pages of this entry explain one by one. A win with no scoring pattern is worth 0 fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.base.co: The $(bold)fan cap$() limits the fan. It is 3 by default, so more than 3 fan still counts as 8 points. The host can change the cap from 0 to 8 fan in the rule settings, and the base points change with it. With a cap of 5, the maximum is 32 points.

On a discard win, the discarder pays the winner the base points. On a self-drawn win, each other player who has not won pays the base points plus the $(bold)self-draw bonus$(), 1 point by default. The bonus can be changed from 0 to 8 points in the rule settings.

For example, a Full Flush is 2 fan, so a discard win collects 4 points. A self-drawn win while nobody has won yet collects 5 points from each of the other three players, 15 in all. If one player has already won and left, it collects 5 points from each of the two remaining players, 10 in all.
As another example, a Full Flush, All Pungs and one Root or Kong add up to 4 fan, which exceeds the default cap, so the hand counts as 3 fan and 8 points, and each payer of a self-drawn win pays 9.

manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.full_fl: $(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Only one suit. It adds to Seven Pairs, Root, All Pungs and other fan. The total is then capped.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.golden_: $(bold)Golden Single Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)After four melds are pung (including kongs), one tile remains in hand and wins as a single wait for the pair. All Pungs also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.kong: $(bold)Kong$()$(br)1 fan each$(br2)MIL SBR 2025 only. Each declared kong scores 1 fan. These fan are separate from the kong payment collected when the kong was declared.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.name: Fan and Base Points
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.robbing: $(bold)Robbing a Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong. The pung stays. Win on a Discard after a Kong does not also count. For an added kong made with a kong’s replacement tile, see $(l:sichuan_kongs)Kong Payments$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.root: $(bold)Root$()$(br)1 fan each$(br2)Each set of all four copies of a tile in the winning hand scores 1 fan. Under MIL SBR 2025, four tiles already declared as a kong count as Kong instead. Under T/TFMJ 01—2024, both count as Root (including Kongs).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.seven_p: $(bold)Seven Pairs$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Seven pairs with no melds. Four identical tiles can form two pairs and also count a Root. All Pungs does not count.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.shoot_a: $(bold)Win on a Discard after a Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on the discard another player makes after a kong. For an added kong made with a kong’s replacement tile, see $(l:sichuan_kongs)Kong Payments$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.under_t: $(bold)Last-Tile Win$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by drawing the last tile of the wall, or on the discard made after that draw. It does not count in the ready check at an exhaustive draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.win_aft: $(bold)Win after Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by drawing the replacement tile after a kong. The fan are counted first. Then each payer adds 1 point for the self-draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_kongs.examp: This section gives numbers for the kong points when a discard after a kong is won on. The four players are A, B, C and D, nobody has won yet, and every winner's hand is worth only 1 fan for the win on a discard after a kong or for robbing the kong, which is 2 points.

Example 1, sharing a call transfer. Under T/TFMJ 01—2024, A collects 5 points from consecutive kongs and then discards a tile on which B and C both win. The 5 points are shared between two winners, who are each to receive 3 points, 6 in all, so A supplies the missing 1 point. A also pays B and C 2 points each for the wins.
Example 2, the two presets compared. A makes a concealed kong (B, C and D pay 2 each), draws the replacement tile and adds a kong (1 each), draws again and discards a tile on which B wins.

Under MIL SBR 2025, the 3 points of the added kong are refunded, A keeps the 6 points of the concealed kong and pays B 2, so A ends at +4, B at 0, and C and D at -2 each. Under T/TFMJ 01—2024, all 9 points go to B and A also pays B 2, so A ends at -2, B at +8, and C and D at -3 each.

Example 3, a won added kong. A makes a concealed kong and collects 6 points, draws the replacement tile and adds a kong, and B wins on the tile being added. Under MIL SBR 2025 this is a win on a discard after a kong. The kong stands but earns nothing, A refunds the 6 points and pays B 2, so A ends at -2, B at +2, and C and D at 0.
Under T/TFMJ 01—2024 it is robbing the kong. The added kong does not stand, A keeps the 6 points and pays B 2, so A ends at +4, B at 0, and C and D at -2 each.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_kongs.kongs: A $(bold)kong$() is a set of four identical tiles, after which you draw a replacement tile from the wall. A concealed kong uses four tiles from your hand on your own turn after drawing.

A kong on a discard uses three tiles from your hand and another player's discard, and the client labels it Discard Kong. An added kong adds the fourth tile to a pung you have already called. No kong is possible once the wall has run out or with void-suit tiles.

A kong pays $(bold)kong points$() at once, apart from the fan, and the table shows the three amounts. An added kong pays only if the added tile is the one just drawn. Both presets use these amounts, and the rule settings can change each.

Kong points may have to be refunded at a draw. See $(l:sichuan_draws)Draws and Checks$(/l). The win on a discard after a kong is covered later in this entry.$(br2)For example, A has called a pung of 5 of Bamboo, draws the fourth one and adds it.

B, C and D pay 1 point each and A collects 3. If D has already won, only B and C pay and A collects 2. If A holds four 7 of Characters and declares a concealed kong, B, C and D pay 2 each and A collects 6. If B discards a 3 of Circles and A kongs it with three in hand, only B pays 2.

Kong|Who pays|Each
Concealed|Other players still in|2
On a discard|The discarder|2
Added|Other players still in|1
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_kongs.name: Kong Payments
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_kongs.robbi: When another player adds a kong, you can win on the tile being added, which is $(bold)robbing the kong$(). Only an added kong can be robbed. Concealed kongs and kongs on discards cannot.

If you rob the kong, the original pung remains, the kong does not stand, no kong points are paid, and the robbed tile goes to you. If several players rob, the player adding the kong pays each of them. The win scores 1 fan. See $(l:sichuan_fan#robbing_kong)Robbing the Kong$(/l).

If nobody robs the kong, it stands and the player draws a replacement tile. After a robbed kong, the player does not draw a replacement tile, and the first player after the last winner who has not won draws next.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_kongs.shoot: A $(bold)win on a discard after a kong$() happens when a player kongs, draws the replacement tile, and then discards a tile on which another player wins. The winner scores 1 fan for it. See $(l:sichuan_fan#shoot_after_kong)Win on a Discard After a Kong$(/l).

The discarder pays the win as usual, while the kong points the discarder collected earlier are handled separately, and the presets differ.$(br2)MIL SBR 2025 refunds only the last kong's points, and each payer takes back what they paid. The points of earlier kongs stay with the discarder.

T/TFMJ 01—2024 transfers all the kong points collected from consecutive kongs to the winner, which is called $(bold)call transfer$(). Kongs are consecutive when each one is made in the turn that follows the previous kong. Any other turn in between breaks the chain.

When several players win on the same discard, the total is shared equally, rounded up for each winner, and the discarder makes up any shortfall. Call transfer is settled apart from the win payments, and transferred kong points are not taken back at a draw.

When an added kong made in the turn of a replacement tile is won on, MIL SBR 2025 treats it as a win on a discard after a kong. The kong stands, earns no points, and the last earlier kong is refunded as above.
T/TFMJ 01—2024 treats it as robbing the kong. The added kong does not stand, and the kong points collected earlier are neither refunded nor transferred. The next section gives numbers.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_passing.pas: The $(bold)passed-win restriction$() limits winning. After you pass up a chance to win, you can win on another player's discard again only for a higher fan.

Three situations start the restriction. You could win on another player's discard but chose Pass, Pung or Kong instead. You could win on a tile another player adds to a kong but chose Pass. Or you discarded a tile on which your hand could have won.

The restriction records the fan of that missed win, after the cap. If it starts again, the highest recorded fan is kept.$(br2)While it lasts, you can win on another player's discard only when its fan, after the cap, is higher than the recorded fan.

With the same or a lower fan, the client does not offer Win. Self-drawn wins are not affected.$(br2)The restriction ends on your next draw, which includes the replacement draw after a kong, or when your hand is no longer ready after one of your discards.

For example, your hand is ready and another player discards a 1-fan win, which you pass. A later discard worth 0 or 1 fan cannot be won on, but one worth 2 fan can. With the default cap of 3 fan, passing a 3-fan win blocks every discard until you draw, because no fan can exceed the cap.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_presets.com: MIL SBR 2025 and T/TFMJ 01—2024 share the settings in the table. The options in which they differ are described in the next section of this entry.

See $(l:sichuan_fan)Fan and Base Points$(/l) for the fan cap and the self-draw bonus, $(l:sichuan_kongs)Kong Payments$(/l) for kong points, $(l:sichuan_draws)Draws and Checks$(/l) for the active flower pig and kong refunds, and $(l:sichuan_dealer)Dealers and Hands$(/l) for the number of hands. Tile exchange is the rule in which players swap three tiles before the game starts. Neither preset nor this mod offers it.

Each of these values can be changed in the rule settings. The fan cap goes from 0 to 8 fan, the self-draw bonus from 0 to 8 points, each of the three kong payments from 0 to 8 points, the active flower pig penalty from 1 to 256 points and the number of hands from 1 to 64.
The options for discards after kongs and for refunding kong points at a draw can be switched individually too. When the options no longer match either preset, the rule settings show custom rules.

manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_presets.dif: MIL SBR 2025 and T/TFMJ 01—2024 differ in five places, and each one corresponds to a switch in the rule settings.$(li)For the first discard, MIL SBR 2025 picks the first void-suit discard when choosing the void suit, and T/TFMJ 01—2024 does not.
See $(l:sichuan_void)Void Suits$(/l).$(li)For kongs and roots, MIL SBR 2025 scores declared kongs as Kong and undeclared sets of four as Root, and T/TFMJ 01—2024 scores both as Root.

See $(l:sichuan_fan)Fan and Base Points$(/l).$(li)For discards after kongs, MIL SBR 2025 refunds only the last kong, and T/TFMJ 01—2024 transfers the kong payments of consecutive kongs to the winner, called call transfer.

See $(l:sichuan_kongs)Kong Payments$(/l).$(li)For an added kong after a kong, when an added kong made in the turn of a replacement tile is won on, MIL SBR 2025 treats it as a win on a discard after a kong and T/TFMJ 01—2024 as robbing the kong.
See Kong Payments too.$(li)For the walls, MIL SBR 2025 builds 14 stacks for East and West and 13 for South and North, and T/TFMJ 01—2024 builds 14 for South and North and 13 for East and West.

The wall of 108 tiles has two tiles per stack and so 54 stacks, which are 14 plus 14 plus 13 plus 13 over the four players. How the wall is built decides only how the physical wall looks and where tiles are taken, and has no effect on scoring. The settings the presets share are in the previous section of this entry.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_tiles.name: Tiles and Presets
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_tiles.prese: A $(bold)rule preset$() is a ready-made set of rule options. Sichuan mahjong offers two rule presets, MIL SBR 2025, the 2025 Sichuan Bloody Rules (SBR) of MIL, and T/TFMJ 01—2024.
T/TFMJ 01—2024 is the group standard Rules of Sichuan Mahjong Competition, published in July 2024 by the Tianfu New Area Mahjong Sports Association.

Both presets play the same way in essentials, with the same 108 tiles, void suits, Blood Battle, ready checks, and base points from fan. They differ in five places, namely the first discard, how kongs and roots are scored, discards after kongs, added kongs after kongs, and the wall.

$(l:sichuan_presets)Preset Differences$(/l) summarizes them, and each entry also names the preset where a rule differs. The host can choose a preset in the rule settings and adjust options such as the fan cap, the kong payments and the number of hands one by one.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_tiles.tiles: $(bold)Sichuan mahjong$() is played by four players with only the three numbered suits Characters, Circles and Bamboo. Each suit has the numbers one to nine in four copies, which makes 108 tiles. There are no honors and no flowers.

Chows are not allowed, so tiles can be called only as pungs and kongs. Each player also chooses one suit as a void suit at the start and has to discard every tile of it before winning, so a winning hand contains only two suits. See $(l:sichuan_void)Void Suits$(/l).

In the deal, each player first takes four tiles three times. The dealer then takes the first and the fifth tile of the next group and each other player takes one of the three tiles between them. The dealer therefore holds 14 tiles and discards first, and the other players hold 13.
After the void suits are set, players draw and discard in turn under the Blood Battle rules until three players have won or the wall runs out. See $(l:sichuan_winning)Wins and Blood Battle$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_void.name: Void Suits
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_void.void: $(bold)Void suit selection$() is the step in which each player chooses one of Characters, Circles and Bamboo as a $(bold)void suit$(), after the deal and before the dealer's first discard. Once chosen, the void suit cannot be changed during the hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_void.void.c: A void suit has three effects. While your hand still holds tiles of your void suit, you can discard only those tiles, including a tile you have just drawn.$(br2)You cannot pung a void-suit tile, and you cannot kong one as a kong on a discard, a concealed kong or an added kong.

You can win only when your hand holds no void-suit tile. All void suits are revealed together, and then the dealer discards first.$(br2)Under MIL SBR 2025, each player also secretly picks the first void-suit tile to discard. You pick one tile from your hand, its suit becomes your void suit, and you must discard that tile first.

If you hold no tile of a suit, you can void it without picking a tile. The picked tile stays hidden. T/TFMJ 01—2024 does not preselect, so you may discard any void-suit tile first.$(br2)A player who breaks the void-suit rule is a flower pig. See $(l:sichuan_draws)Draws and Checks$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_winning.bat: $(bold)Blood Battle$() is how a hand of Sichuan mahjong is played. A player who wins leaves the hand, and the others keep drawing and discarding until three players have won or the wall runs out.

A player who has won no longer draws or discards, cannot call or win again, pays nothing and collects no kong payments. The others continue in turn order, skipping players who have won, and after a win the first player after the last winner who has not won draws next.
Several players can win on the same discard. All of them win, and the discarder pays each of them separately.

A hand ends at once when three players have won, with no ready check. If the wall runs out with fewer than three winners, the players still in the hand take a ready check. See $(l:sichuan_draws)Draws and Checks$(/l).$(br2)For example, A discards a tile on which both B (1 fan, 2 points) and C (2 fan, 4 points) can win.

Both win, and A pays B 2 points and C 4 points. D draws next. Two players have won, so A and D play on, and the hand ends when one more of them wins. A also deals the next hand, because the discarder deals when several players win on the same discard. See $(l:sichuan_dealer)Dealers and Hands$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_winning.exa: Four identical tiles as two pairs, which also scores a Root.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_winning.sha: The $(bold)winning shape$() is the way the hand and the called tiles together make a win, either four melds and a pair or seven pairs. A meld is a sequence or a triplet, and a kong counts as a triplet. The pair is two identical tiles.

Concealed tiles can form sequences, but because chows cannot be called, called melds are always pungs or kongs. Seven pairs consists of seven pairs with no called tiles, and four identical tiles can count as two pairs.

There is no minimum fan, so a hand without any scoring pattern, worth 0 fan, can win. See $(l:sichuan_fan)Fan and Base Points$(/l) for fan and points. Only two restrictions apply. The hand must hold no void-suit tile, see $(l:sichuan_void)Void Suits$(/l). After you pass up a win you can win on another player's discard only for a higher fan, see $(l:sichuan_passing)Passed Wins$(/l).

Winning on a tile you drew is $(bold)self-drawn$(), and a replacement tile after a kong counts as drawn. Winning on another player's discard is a discard win, and the player who discarded it is the $(bold)discarder$(). You can also win on the tile another player adds to a kong, which is robbing the kong.

See $(l:sichuan_kongs)Kong Payments$(/l). After a self-drawn win, each other player still in the hand pays. After a discard win, the discarder pays. The amounts are in $(l:sichuan_fan)Fan and Base Points$(/l). When you can win, the client offers the Win action.

manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_calls.calls: A $(bold)call$() takes another player's discard and forms a meld in front of you with tiles from your hand. A $(bold)chow$() takes the discard of the previous player, the one right before you in turn order, and forms a sequence with two tiles from your hand.
For example, with 4, 5, 7 and 8 of Characters in hand, the previous player's 6 of Characters can be chowed with 4-5, 5-7 or 7-8. A $(bold)pung$() takes any player's discard and forms a triplet with two identical tiles. An $(bold)open kong$() takes any player's discard and forms a kong with three identical tiles.

After each discard, the other three players each choose to win, call or pass. When several players claim the same tile, a win beats a pung or kong, and a pung or kong beats a chow. If several players claim a win, the first in turn order after the discarder wins.

For example, the next player wants to chow a 5 of Circles and the player across wants to pung it. The pung goes ahead. After a chow or pung you draw nothing and discard at once, and play continues in turn order. If nobody calls, the next player after the discarder draws.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_calls.kongs: A $(bold)kong$() is four identical tiles, made in three ways. An $(bold)open kong$() takes another player's discard and adds three identical tiles from your hand. Like a pung, it outranks a chow. A $(bold)concealed kong$() uses four identical tiles in your hand. An $(bold)added kong$() adds the tile you just drew to a pung you already made.
Concealed and added kongs are declared only on your own turn, right after drawing. Every kong takes a replacement tile from the back of the wall, and you then discard. A kong needs a tile to replace it. The default Wall Reserve needs at least two drawable tiles, and the fixed reserve at least one. See $(l:taiwan_tiles)Tiles and the Deal$(/l).

When a player declares an added kong, the other three may win on the tile being added. This is $(l:taiwan_tai#robbing_kong)Robbing a Kong$(/l), and the player declaring the kong pays. Concealed kongs cannot be robbed. The added kong stands only if nobody robs it.
Once no tile can be drawn any more, the last discard can only be won, not called. After you declare ready you can no longer chow, pung or kong. See $(l:taiwan_ready)Declaring Ready$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_calls.name: Calls and Kongs
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flowers.flow: A $(bold)flower replacement$() reveals a flower tile and takes a replacement tile from the back of the wall. Flowers never form melds and do not count toward the 17 tiles of a winning hand. Only the Pocket Common wall contains flowers. Southern Common has no replacements.

The $(bold)opening replacement$() takes place after the deal and before the first discard, starting with the dealer and following turn order. Each player in turn reveals every flower in hand, which stay face up until the hand ends, and takes the same number of tiles from the back of the wall.

A replacement that is another flower waits until all four players have finished the round and is replaced in the next round. The opening replacement ends after a round in which nobody reveals a flower. For example, the dealer reveals two flowers and takes an ordinary tile and a flower. The new flower waits for the next round.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flowers.name: Flowers
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flowers.play: A flower drawn during play is replaced at once. It is revealed and a replacement is taken from the back of the wall, again and again until an ordinary tile arrives. Each replacement leaves one tile fewer to draw, and if no tile is left the hand ends in a draw. See $(l:taiwan_tiles)Tiles and the Deal$(/l).

Revealed flowers can score. A flower matching your seat wind scores 1 tai as a $(l:taiwan_tai#seat_flower)Seat Flower$(/l). A complete set of spring, summer, autumn and winter, or of plum, orchid, chrysanthemum and bamboo, scores 1 tai as a $(l:taiwan_tai#flower_set)Flower Set$(/l).

Under Pocket Common, a self-draw win on a tile drawn after a flower replacement scores $(l:taiwan_tai#replacement_win)Replacement Win$(/l). Holding all eight flowers, or seven while another player holds the last, wins automatically as a flower win. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Payments and Repeats$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_passing.lift: A passed-win restriction is lifted in two ways. First, you discard a tile that was not among your waits just before the draw, or before the chow or pung if you called. Second, you complete an added kong. Discarding one of those waits leaves the restriction in place.
For example, you wait on 3 and 6 of Bamboo, and East discards a 3 of Bamboo. You pass, so the restriction applies. South then discards a 6 of Bamboo, and you cannot win.

You then draw a 9 of Characters and discard it. It is not one of your waits, so the restriction ends, and a 3 or 6 of Bamboo wins again. Had you drawn a 6 of Bamboo, you could not win with it, and discarding it would not lift the restriction.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_passing.name: Passed Wins
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_passing.pass: A $(bold)passed-win restriction$() applies after you pass up a win. On your own turn, you draw a tile that would win but discard or declare a kong instead. Or another player discards a tile you could win on, and you choose Pass, chow, pung or kong instead of Win.

While the restriction applies, the Win option does not appear. You cannot win on a discard, cannot rob a kong and cannot win by self-draw, but you can still discard and call as usual. Drawing a tile does not lift the restriction, even if it is one of your winning tiles. Flower wins are not affected. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Payments and Repeats$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.amo: $(bold)Calculating Win Payments$()$(br2)Each player's payment is base + tai × points per tai. The base is a fixed number of points included in each payment. By default, the base is 1 point and each tai is worth 1 point.

Add only patterns that can score together. Concealed Self-Draw is 3 tai and replaces separate awards for Concealed Hand and Self-Draw. See $(l:taiwan_tai)Tai Patterns$(/l) for the conditions. Payments involving the dealer also include $(l:taiwan_payments#dealer)Dealer Tai and Repeat Tai$(/l).
The host can change the base, points per tai, dealer tai and tai per repeat under Scoring and Payments in the rule settings.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.dea: $(bold)Dealer Tai and Repeat Tai$()$(br2)For a win on a discard, add dealer tai and repeat tai if either the winner or the discarder is the dealer. If both are nondealers, neither addition applies.
When the dealer self-draws, all three nondealers add dealer tai and repeat tai to their payments. When a nondealer self-draws, only the dealer adds these tai; the other two nondealers do not.
Pocket Common awards 1 dealer tai plus 2 tai for each repeat. One repeat is called 連一拉一 and two repeats 連二拉二. These add 3 tai and 5 tai respectively, including the dealer tai.

Example: under Pocket Common, the dealer has repeated once. A nondealer self-draws for 3 tai, including the self-draw award but excluding dealer and repeat tai. The other nondealers pay 1 + 3 = 4 points each; the dealer pays 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 = 7 points. The winner receives 15 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.flo: $(bold)Flower Wins: Eight Flowers and Seven Robbing One$()$(br2)Pocket Common allows automatic wins based on flower tiles without a standard winning hand of five melds and a pair. A flower win cannot be declined and is not blocked by a passed-win restriction.

$(li)Eight Flowers: holding all eight flowers scores 8 tai, paid by the other three players as a self-draw.$(li)Seven Robbing One: holding seven flowers while another player holds the eighth scores 8 tai, paid only by the holder of that last flower.

During play, drawing a seventh or eighth flower requires completing the flower replacement before checking the flower win. If a player already holds seven flowers when another draws the eighth, Seven Robbing One takes effect immediately. The player drawing the eighth flower does not replace it and pays the winner.
During the initial flower replacement, wait until every player has finished replacing flowers. Flower wins are then checked in turn order, starting with the dealer.

If the replacement also completes a standard winning hand, score its tai separately from the flower win. The standard self-draw is paid by the other three players; the flower win determines its own paying players. A player paying for both includes the base only once. Add dealer and repeat tai according to each player's role.

Example: a nondealer draws a seventh flower and wins on its replacement. The ordinary win totals 5 tai before flower-win and dealer additions. Another nondealer holds the eighth flower; the dealer has not repeated. The flower holder pays 1 + 5 + 8 = 14 points, the dealer pays 1 + 5 + 1 = 7 points, and the remaining nondealer pays 1 + 5 = 6 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.pay: $(bold)Who Pays$()$(br2)For a win on a discard, only the discarder pays the winner. For robbing a kong, the player declaring the added kong pays. For a self-draw, the other three players each pay the winner. An exhaustive draw requires no payments. Declaring a kong earns no points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.pre: $(bold)Differences Between Pocket Common and Southern Common$()$(br2)Both presets collect common ways of playing; neither is the uniform rule of a region. Southern Common differs from Pocket Common as follows, and its other tai patterns and values are the same:

$(li)It uses 136 tiles without flowers, so it has no flower wins, Seat Flowers or Flower Sets.$(li)Single Wait scores no tai.$(li)The dealer’s own 1 tai is not added, but each repeat still adds 2 tai: 2 tai for one repeat and 4 tai for two.

$(li)Hand tai are capped at 4, so a larger hand counts as 4 tai. Dealer tai and repeat tai are added outside the cap.$(br2)Example: under Southern Common, the dealer has repeated once and self-draws a hand normally worth 8 tai. It counts as 4 tai, and each of the other three players pays 1 + 4 + 2 = 7 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.rep: $(bold)Dealer Repeats and the End of the Match$()$(br2)If the dealer wins or the hand ends in an exhaustive draw, the dealer deals again.
This is a dealer repeat, and the repeat count increases by one. If a nondealer wins, the dealer’s next player in turn order becomes dealer and the count returns to zero.

A match has four rounds, East, South, West and North, and each player deals once per round: sixteen dealer positions in all. The fourth North dealer can still repeat; the match ends when that dealer passes the deal. Scores start at zero and accumulate. A negative score does not end the match.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.res: $(bold)Payments on the Results Screen$()$(br2)The results screen lists the winner’s tai patterns and tai, then one line for each player’s payment to the winner, with the base, hand tai and dealer tai in parentheses.
Flower-win tai count as hand tai, and repeat tai count as dealer tai. After an exhaustive draw, the title reads Exhaustive draw and no payments are listed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_ready.declar: After you declare ready, you can no longer chow, pung or kong, and when another player discards you can only win or pass. On your own turn you either win or discard the tile you just drew, so your hand no longer changes.

Declaring early scores more. If nobody has called a chow, pung or kong yet, the dealer declaring on the first discard scores $(l:taiwan_tai#heavenly_ready)Heavenly Ready$(/l) at 16 tai, and a nondealer declaring on their own first discard scores $(l:taiwan_tai#earthly_ready)Earthly Ready$(/l) at 8 tai. Each replaces the 1 tai of Declared Ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_ready.name: Declaring Ready
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_ready.ready: A hand is $(bold)ready$() when one more tile would complete it, and the tiles that would complete it are its waits. To $(bold)declare ready$(), discard a tile on your own turn that leaves your hand ready. Declaring is optional, but a win after declaring scores 1 more tai as Declared Ready.
Click the Declare Ready button, then click a highlighted tile to discard it and declare. Right-click or press Esc to cancel. See $(l:controls)Table Controls$(/l). Declaring does not need a concealed hand, and afterwards the seat information shows Ready Declared.

For example, you hold 123, 456 and 789 of Characters, 234 of Circles, a pair of 5 Bamboo and 6-7 Bamboo, and draw a 9 of Circles. Discarding it leaves a hand waiting on 5 and 8 of Bamboo, so you can declare.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.all_from: $(bold)All from Others$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)All five melds are chows, pungs or open kongs, and the pair is completed on another player’s discard or a robbed kong tile. Not counted with a concealed kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.all_hono: $(bold)All Honors$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Only honors. Does not count All Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.all_trip: $(bold)All Triplets$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Five pungs (including kongs) and a pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.big_four: $(bold)Big Four Winds$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of East, South, West and North. Round Wind and Seat Wind are also counted when they apply.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.big_thre: $(bold)Big Three Dragons$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of Red, Green and White. Does not count Red Dragon, Green Dragon, White Dragon.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.combinin: The tai of a hand are worked out in three steps. First, find every pattern the winning hand meets. Several can apply at once. Second, add their values. A pattern counted per tile or per set, such as Seat Flower and Flower Set, adds its value once for each.

Third, remove excluded patterns. When a pattern says it does not count other patterns, those are removed whenever it applies. For example, a concealed self-drawn win with a Half Flush and a pung of Red Dragons scores Concealed Self-Draw 3, Half Flush 4 and Red Dragon 1, 8 tai in all.

When a hand can be split into melds in more than one way, the split with the most tai is used. A hand that meets no pattern still wins and scores 0 tai. Exclusions prevent counting the same feature twice. Concealed Self-Draw already contains Concealed Hand and Self-Draw, so they are not added again.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.conceale: $(bold)Concealed Hand$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on another player's discard or on a robbed kong tile without having called a chow, pung or open kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. A concealed self-drawn win scores Concealed Self-Draw instead. Concealed Hand is not counted.
$(bold)Concealed Self-Draw$()$(br)3 tai$(br2)Concealed only, winning by self-draw. Does not count Concealed Hand, Self-Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.declared: $(bold)Declared Ready$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win after declaring ready. Declaring ready does not require a concealed hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.earthly_: $(bold)Earthly Ready$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)A nondealer declares ready on their first discard, before anyone has called a chow, pung or kong, and later wins the hand. Does not count Declared Ready.
$(bold)Earthly Hand$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)A nondealer wins by self-draw on their first draw, before anyone has called a chow, pung or kong. Does not count Concealed Self-Draw, Concealed Hand, Self-Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.eight_fl: $(bold)Eight Flowers$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)An automatic flower win with all eight flowers. No winning shape is needed. Does not count Seat Flower, Flower Set. Pocket Common only. Payment is covered in Payments and Repeats.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.five_con: $(bold)Five Concealed Triplets$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Five concealed pungs (including concealed kongs). A pung completed on another player’s discard is not concealed. Does not count Four and Three Concealed Triplets. All Triplets also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.flower_s: $(bold)Flower Set$()$(br)1 tai per set$(br2)A complete set of spring, summer, autumn and winter, or of plum, orchid, chrysanthemum and bamboo. Each set scores 1 tai. Pocket Common only. Not counted with a flower win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.four_con: $(bold)Four Concealed Triplets$()$(br)5 tai$(br2)Four concealed pungs (including concealed kongs). Does not count Three Concealed Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.full_flu: $(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Only one suit, with no honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.green_dr: $(bold)Green Dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of Green.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.half_flu: $(bold)Half Flush$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Only one suit plus honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.half_fro: $(bold)Half from Others$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)All five melds are chows, pungs or open kongs, and the pair is completed by self-draw. Not counted with a concealed kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.heavenly: $(bold)Heavenly Ready$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)The dealer declares ready on their first discard, before anyone has called a chow, pung or kong, and later wins the hand. Does not count Concealed Hand, Declared Ready.

$(bold)Heavenly Hand$()$(br)24 tai$(br2)After replacing flowers, the dealer’s dealt hand is already complete, before anyone has called a chow, pung or kong. Does not count Concealed Self-Draw, Concealed Hand, Self-Draw, Replacement Win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.human_wi: $(bold)Human Hand$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)A nondealer wins on another player’s first discard before the dealer’s second discard, with no chow, pung or kong called by anyone and without having declared ready. Does not count Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.intro: $(bold)Tai$() are the unit that measures the value of a winning hand. A $(bold)tai pattern$() is a feature of the winning hand, such as a flush or a self-draw, and each pattern is worth a fixed number of tai. This entry lists the conditions and tai of every pattern.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.intro.co: The value on each card is for that pattern alone, not for the whole hand. Pocket Common sets no limit on hand tai. Southern Common does not score Single Wait and caps hand tai at 4. Dealer tai and repeat tai are added on top. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Payments and Repeats$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.last_dis: $(bold)Last Discard$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on the discard made by the player who drew the last drawable tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.last_dra: $(bold)Last Draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win by self-draw on the last drawable tile. Reserved tiles are not drawable.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.name: Tai Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.pinfu: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Five chows and a suited pair, with no honors or flowers, won on another player’s discard or a robbed kong tile. No two-sided wait is required. Under Pocket Common, Single Wait also counts when it applies.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.red_drag: $(bold)Red Dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of Red.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.replacem: $(bold)Replacement Win$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win by self-draw on a replacement tile. Pocket Common counts replacements for kongs and flowers. Southern Common counts only kong replacements. Apply Self-Draw or Concealed Self-Draw according to their conditions, without counting both.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.robbing_: $(bold)Robbing a Kong$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong. Concealed kongs cannot be robbed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.round_wi: $(bold)Round Wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of the round wind. Round Wind and Seat Wind both count when they are the same wind.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.seat_flo: $(bold)Seat Flower$()$(br)1 tai per flower$(br2)Flower numbers 1 to 4 correspond to East, South, West and North. Spring and plum are 1, summer and orchid 2, autumn and chrysanthemum 3, winter and bamboo 4. Each flower matching your seat wind scores 1 tai. Pocket Common only. Not counted with a flower win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.seat_win: $(bold)Seat Wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of your seat wind. Each hand, seat winds run East, South, West and North from the dealer.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.self_dra: $(bold)Self-Draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on a tile you draw yourself. A concealed self-drawn win counts Concealed Self-Draw instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.seven_ro: $(bold)Seven Robbing One$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)An automatic flower win when you hold seven flowers and another player holds the last one. No winning shape is needed. Does not count Seat Flower, Flower Set. Pocket Common only. Payment is covered in Payments and Repeats.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.single_w: $(bold)Single Wait$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)The whole hand waits on only one kind of tile. Edge, closed or single waits all qualify, and the tile you wait on need not be its last remaining copy. Not scored under Southern Common.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.small_fo: $(bold)Small Four Winds$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of three winds with the fourth wind as the pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.small_th: $(bold)Small Three Dragons$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of two dragons with the third dragon as the pair. Does not count Red Dragon, Green Dragon, White Dragon.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.three_co: $(bold)Three Concealed Triplets$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Three concealed pungs (including concealed kongs). A pung completed on another player’s discard is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.white_dr: $(bold)White Dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of White.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.deal: The $(bold)deal$() gives each player a starting hand. After the wall is built, the dice decide where the first tile is taken. Starting with the $(bold)dealer$() and following turn order (counterclockwise), each player takes four tiles per round for four rounds, ending with 16.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.deal.c: The dealer then draws a 17th tile and discards first. The other three players are $(bold)nondealers$().$(br2)After the deal, players replace their flowers. See $(l:taiwan_flowers)Flowers$(/l). Then the dealer discards. From then on, draws come from the front of the wall, and replacements for flowers and kongs come from the back.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.exampl: Five melds and a pair make seventeen tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.name: Tiles and the Deal
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.reserv: The $(bold)reserve$() is a block of tiles at the back of the wall that cannot be drawn, so that flower and kong replacements always have tiles left. Reserved tiles cannot be drawn or used for replacements. The wall minus the reserve is the number of tiles that can still be drawn.

The host chooses the reserve size with Wall Reserve in the rule settings, which offers the two options in the table.$(br2)When a player must draw or take a replacement and no tile can be drawn, the hand ends in a draw with no winner. No one pays, and the dealer repeats. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Payments and Repeats$(/l).

For example, under Southern Common the wall has 136 tiles, the deal takes 65 and the reserve holds 16, so 55 tiles can be drawn. With the default option, each completed kong takes one replacement tile and adds one to the reserve, so two fewer tiles can be drawn.

Wall Reserve|Reserve size
Reserve: 16 Tiles, Plus 1 per Kong|The default. Starts at 16 and grows by one for each completed kong
Reserve: 16 Tiles|Stays at 16 tiles
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.shape: A $(bold)win$() is a complete hand, and it ends the hand at once. A standard hand has five melds and a pair. A $(bold)meld$() is a group of three tiles. A $(bold)sequence$() is three consecutive tiles of one suit, and a $(bold)triplet$() is three identical tiles.
Four identical tiles form a $(bold)kong$(), also one meld. Winds and dragons form only triplets, kongs or pairs. A $(bold)pair$() is two identical tiles.$(br2)Without kongs, the winning hand has 17 tiles.

Five melds make 15 and the pair makes 2, which is the 16 tiles in hand plus the winning tile. For example, 123, 456 and 789 Characters and 234 and 567 Circles, plus a pair of 5 Bamboo, make 17 tiles. Each kong adds one tile. Count tiles set aside after calls and concealed kongs, but not exposed flowers.

Winning on a tile you drew is $(bold)self-drawn$(). When you win on another player's discard, the player who discarded it is the $(bold)discarder$(). A win has no minimum tai. Any complete hand wins, and tai only decide the score. See $(l:taiwan_tai)Tai Patterns$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tiles.tiles: $(bold)Taiwanese mahjong$() is played by four players, each holding 16 tiles, and a win needs five melds and a pair. The wall has 136 ordinary tiles, four copies of each, which are the Characters, Circles and Bamboo from 1 to 9 making 108 tiles and the four winds and three dragons making 28.
$(bold)Flowers$() are eight further tiles, namely spring, summer, autumn and winter, and plum, orchid, chrysanthemum and bamboo. Pocket Common adds them to the wall for 144 tiles. Southern Common uses no flowers. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Payments and Repeats$(/l) for the two rule presets.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.backs: The sixteen vanilla dyes change the color of tile backs. Put a dye in the box’s dye slot and click the Dye backs button to recolor every tile in the box for one dye. With Undo Dye in the slot, the same button removes the back color.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.backs.continu: One dye can also color tiles, a mahjong box, a table cloth or a mahjong stool. The diagram shows a table cloth.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.blanks: Tiles start as blanks without faces. Blanks can be cut from any kind of wooden planks, or from bone blocks, quartz blocks, calcite, glass or amethyst blocks, and their material matches the source.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.blanks.contin: Right-click while holding a mahjong box to open it. The box has slots for tiles and point sticks, a dye slot and a dice slot.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.name: Making Mahjong Tiles
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.printing: Printing faces and backs on blanks uses Mahjong Dye.$(br2)Put 136 or 144 blanks of one material in a mahjong box and place Mahjong Dye in the dye slot.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.printing.cont: Choose a face preset and a back preset in the preview, then click the Apply button to print the whole set at once for one Mahjong Dye. A 144-tile set includes eight flowers.$(br2)Mahjong Dye can also change the face or back preset of a printed set.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.red_fives: $(bold)Red Dora Dye$() turns an ordinary 5 of Characters, Circles or Bamboo into the matching Red Five, and $(bold)Undo Dye$() turns a Red Five back into an ordinary 5.$(br2)A Red Five is a 5 with a red face, and it counts as a dora in rules that use red fives.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.red_fives.con: The table checks at the start of a match that the mahjong box holds as many Red Fives as the chosen rules need. See the set requirements later in this entry.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.sets: When a match starts, the table picks one mahjong box from its storage. The box must hold a complete set whose material, face and back all match. Spare tiles can stay in the box.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.sets.continue: Four-player Riichi mahjong needs 136 tiles, and three-player mahjong, which omits the 2 to 8 of Characters, needs 108. Sichuan mahjong uses only Characters, Circles and Bamboo, also 108 tiles.

MCR and Pocket Common in Taiwanese mahjong also need eight different flowers. When the rules use Red Fives, they replace ordinary 5s of the same suit in the same box. The Table Preparation screen in the lobby lists anything missing.
manual.mchjong.landing: This manual explains how to set up tables, prepare tiles and play, and covers the rules of Riichi, MCR, Sichuan and Taiwanese mahjong.$(br2)Click a category icon on the right page or type a keyword in the search box.
manual.mchjong.name: Mahjong Handbook
manual.mchjong.recommend.text: Install the optional Patchouli mod to read the Mahjong Handbook in-game. Please download the file matching your Minecraft version and mod loader.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_1: Put the tiles your rules need into the box. Use 136 for four players or 108 for three, all with matching material, backs, and face preset. Spare tiles may stay in the box.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_2: Right-click the table to open its storage. It holds up to two boxes.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_3: Right-click the table with a cloth in hand to drape it. With the cloth down and a full set ready, you can start preparing a match.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_4: Open the side drawer to store every stick denomination and pay players manually during settlement.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_5: While waiting, move boxes in and out through the storage screen. Keep both hands empty and sneak-right-click the tabletop to retrieve the cloth.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_1: Leave a clear 3 × 3 area for the table, with nothing blocking the space above.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_2: Place the table in the center of the area. Its rim reaches into the surrounding blocks.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_3: Put one stool two blocks from the center on each side you play on.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_4: Both ordinary and automatic tables use this compact layout.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_1: Right-click a stool to sit down and open the table screen. Right-click the stool again while seated to reopen it.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_2: Pick a three- or four-player preset in the lobby, then have everyone click Ready.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_3: On ordinary tables, sweep the loose tiles to shuffle, drag stacks in front of you to build the wall, then drag tiles from the wall into your hand.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_4: Automatic tables shuffle, build walls, deal, and draw all by themselves.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_5: Click a table tile to discard it. The screen lists the chi, pon, kan, riichi, and win options available right now.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_6: Close the screen and you can look around while staying seated. Press sneak to stand up.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_1: Use a mixer and basin to dye two stacks of tiles, two boxes of tiles, or one of each with a single dye. Each full stack or box counts as one. For example, two boxes and one blue dye turn the backs of both sets blue.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_2: Only the backs change. Faces, red fives, material, names, sticks, and dice stay untouched. Glass tiles turn into stained glass.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_3: One Undo Dye removes the back color from two tile stacks or boxes. Both must have a back color that the dye can remove. If either would remain unchanged, the machine will not run or consume the dye.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_4: A deployer applies Red Dora Dye to 5m, 5p, and 5s tiles one by one on belts or depots. Undo Dye restores them one by one, keeping the back color.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_5: A mixer marks 16 identical blank sticks with a single dye. Use white for 100, blue for 1,000, yellow for 5,000, red for 10,000, and black for −10,000 points.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_production.text_: A mechanical saw cuts 24 blank tiles from each block of material. Six blocks make 144 tiles. A bone block can also be cut into 32 blank point sticks.
Mix black, red, green, blue, and white dye for two Mahjong Dyes. One red dye blends into eight Red Dora Dyes, and one black dye into eight Undo Dyes.
To make a mahjong box, use a deployer to attach leather to a chest, then attach an iron nugget. Finish by pressing it with a mechanical press. This recipe does not need wooden slabs.
Under a mechanical press, place an empty box, 144 identical blank tiles, one Mahjong Dye, and a printing plate, and the machine prints Kansai faces.
The press outputs the full 144-tile box and returns the plate. Send the plate back for the next batch. Material, backs, and names are kept.

A press and basin can also pack tiles, marked point sticks, and dice into a mahjong box. Each type of item must fit in its usual slots, just as when you pack the box by hand. The packed box can go straight into the table.

room.mchjong.equipment.bust_sticks.descr: When bankruptcy does not end the match, put one −10000-point stick per seat in the mahjong boxes.
room.mchjong.equipment.case.description: Put a complete tile case in the table. Cases are checked separately.
room.mchjong.equipment.cloth.description: Place a tablecloth on the table.
room.mchjong.equipment.debt_cards.descri: Put one −500-point debt card per player in the mahjong boxes: four debt cards in total.
room.mchjong.equipment.dice.description: Ordinary tables require two dice stored in their cases, or three dice for Taiwanese mahjong.
room.mchjong.equipment.drawer_space.desc: Drawers may hold only the payment supplies this variant uses. Leave space in each drawer for the starting supplies and the reserve bust stick or debt card.
room.mchjong.equipment.face.description: The selected set must share one face design.
room.mchjong.equipment.flowers.descripti: These rules require all eight distinct flowers in the same case as the ordinary tiles.
room.mchjong.equipment.invalid_case.desc: Check the case slots and item counts.
room.mchjong.equipment.material.descript: The selected set must use one tile material. Spare tiles are allowed.
room.mchjong.equipment.point_sticks.desc: The cases must contain the required number of point sticks in each denomination for every seat’s starting score.
room.mchjong.equipment.red_fives.descrip: One case must contain all the red fives required by the selected setting.
room.mchjong.equipment.scoring_cards.des: Put four 500-point kits in the boxes. Each kit needs one 100-point scoring card, four 50-point scoring cards, ten 10-point scoring cards, ten 8-point scoring cards and twenty 1-point scoring cards.
room.mchjong.equipment.tiles.description: One case must contain every ordinary tile required by the selected rules. Red fives cannot replace ordinary fives.
